punctuated: 聖智之高明也。臣請得為陛下言之。盖自邇年以来，文臣則或因開貢之條而混升國學，或緣納粟之例而濫登仕籍，况夫拘於資格之先後，牽於歷任之久近，以有限之職，待雜進之流，銓衡之途由之壅矣。武將則勲舊是屬，而秉節鉞者或韜畧之蔑聞；弊習相承，而統師旅者或勤能之罕著。况夫功多出於賄求，賞每加於倖得，未經鋒鏑之勞，巳登録用之典，衛所之員由之濫矣。銓衡之途既壅，何敢望其展素蘊以理民？衛所之員既濫，何敢望其奮武勇以馭兵哉？此不能無勞於聖慮也。為今之計，莫若嚴考察黜陟之法：治行卓異者，則增秩以獎異之；年力衰邁者，則以禮而退遣之；杜塞奔競僥倖之門，擯斥庸陋貪汚之輩，則用人之道，必如唐臣陸贄所謂「名利相均」而不至於壅矣。重爵賞勸懲之典：功勲既著者，則計其勞以加賞；材畧有聞者，則隨其能以授任；不以其無功而施汎濫之恩，不以其有罪而行姑息之政，則選將之要，必如唐臣陸贄所謂「虚實相濟」而不至於濫矣。盖誘人之方，惟名與利，名近虚而於教為重，利近實而於德為輕，錫貨財、賦秩廩，所以彰其實；差品列、殊章服，所以飾其虚；
translation_en:
…the lofty brilliance of Your Sacred Wisdom. Your servant begs leave to speak of this for Your Majesty.

In recent years, among civil officials, some have indiscriminately ascended to the National University through regulations opening up tribute-student quotas, while others have excessively entered the official registers by way of rules permitting the contribution of grain. Moreover, bound by the precedence of qualifications and constrained by the length of tenure in office, a finite number of posts are used to await a motley stream of entrants; because of this, the path of personnel evaluation and appointment has become clogged. As for military commanders, appointments go to those of old merit and established families, so that those who wield the emblems and battle-axes of command have sometimes never heard of strategic arts; corrupt practices are passed down, so that those who lead army brigades rarely display diligence or ability. Furthermore, merit mostly comes from bribery and solicitation, and rewards are repeatedly bestowed upon those who obtain them by lucky chance. Before they have undergone the toil of blade and arrowhead, they are already entered into the statutes for appointment and employment; because of this, the personnel of the Guards and Battalions have become excessive. Once the path of personnel evaluation and appointment is clogged, how can one dare hope that officials will unfold their cherished learning to govern the people? Once the personnel of the Guards and Battalions are excessive, how can one dare hope that commanders will rouse martial valor to command the troops? This cannot but trouble Your Sacred Thoughts.

As a plan for the present, nothing is better than strictly enforcing the laws of evaluation, demotion, and promotion. For those whose administrative conduct is outstanding, increase their rank to reward and distinguish them; for those whose age and vigor are declining, dismiss them with courtesy. Close off the gates ofopportunistic competition and lucky advancement, and reject the mediocre, vile, greedy, and corrupt. Then the way of employing men will surely be what the Tang official Lu Zhi 陸贄 called "balancing name and profit," and will not become clogged. Give weight to the statutes of noble rank, reward, encouragement, and punishment. For those whose merit and achievement are already manifest, calculate their toil in order to bestow additional rewards; for those whose talent and strategy are renowned, grant them offices according to their capabilities. Do not dispense indiscriminate grace where there is no merit, and do not practice indulgent governance where there is guilt. Then the essential principle of selecting commanders will surely be what the Tang official Lu Zhi called "making the nominal and the substantial complement each other," and will not become excessive.

For the means of motivating men lie solely in name and profit. Name approaches the nominal, yet in moral instruction it carries weight; profit approaches the substantial, yet in virtue it is light. Bestowing goods and wealth and granting salaried stipends are the means to manifest the substantial; grading official ranks and distinguishing insignia and vestments are the means to adorn the nominal…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
虛實交相養故人不瀆輕重互相制故國不廢權
疏通之術豈越於此乎然求其本則在於
陛下此心之誠而已誠心以行之而必期其功則司理民
之責者皆有守有為之人當馭兵之寄者咸有嚴有
翼之士尚何慮其有不疏通者哉雨露適時則年豐
旱澇相仍則年歉此歲無常稔者乃天之道久居其
地則難棄久享其利則重遷此土有常懷者乃人之
情然堯雖有洪水滔天而黎民之於變者自若由其
有以備天道之無常湯雖有大旱積久而商邑之用
協者自如由其有以遂人情之常懷天時地利在人
===
裁制不可不知也我
國家救荒有法儲蓄有備而所以因天時者得其道矣
田有等則賦無過取而所以因地利者得其道矣糴
之價奚至於貴民之居奚至於徙乎仰惟
陛下有懷保小民之心有萬邦咸寧之效然猶深求至治
以天時地利為生民之所資故欲有以財成之此尤
見
聖心之剛健也臣請得為
陛下陳之蓋自邇年以來年一歉則穀粟缺乏無以給民
食囊橐空虛無以遂民生而啼飢號寒者深可矜也

punctuated:
虛實交相養，故人不瀆；輕重互相制，故國不廢權。疏通之術，豈越於此乎？然求其本，則在於陛下此心之誠而已。誠心以行之，而必期其功，則司理民之責者，皆有守有為之人；當馭兵之寄者，咸有嚴有翼之士。尚何慮其有不疏通者哉？

雨露適時則年豐，旱澇相仍則年歉，此歲無常稔者，乃天之道；久居其地則難棄，久享其利則重遷，此土有常懷者，乃人之情。然堯雖有洪水滔天，而黎民之於變者自若，由其有以備天道之無常；湯雖有大旱積久，而商邑之用協者自如，由其有以遂人情之常懷。天時地利，在人裁制，不可不知也。我國家救荒有法，儲蓄有備，而所以因天時者得其道矣；田有等則，賦無過取，而所以因地利者得其道矣。糴之價奚至於貴？民之居奚至於徙乎？仰惟陛下有懷保小民之心，有萬邦咸寧之效，然猶深求至治，以天時地利為生民之所資，故欲有以財成之，此尤見聖心之剛健也。臣請得為陛下陳之。蓋自邇年以來，年一歉則穀粟缺乏，無以給民食，囊橐空虛，無以遂民生，而啼飢號寒者，深可矜也；
translation_en:
When the nominal and the substantive mutually nourish one another, people do not grow presumptuous; when the light and the heavy mutually check one another, the state does not lose its authority to weigh and adjust. How could the art of keeping channels open and unobstructed go beyond this? Yet if we seek its root, it lies simply in the sincerity of Your Majesty's own heart. If you carry it out with a sincere heart and insist upon actual results, then those charged with the responsibility of governing the people will all be men of integrity and capability, and those entrusted with the command of troops will all be officers of strictness and reverence. What worry would there still be that anything might remain obstructed?

When rain and dew come at the proper time, the year is bountiful; when drought and flood follow upon one another, the year is lean. That harvests are not perpetually abundant is the Way of Heaven. When people have long dwelled in a place, it is hard for them to abandon it; when they have long enjoyed its benefits, they are reluctant to relocate. That people harbor a constant attachment to their native soil is human nature. Yet although Yao faced floodwaters that swelled to heaven, the transformation of the black-haired people proceeded as before, because he had the means to prepare against the inconstancy of the Way of Heaven; and although Tang faced a great and prolonged drought, the harmony of the capital of Shang remained intact, because he had the means to fulfill the constant attachment of human nature. One cannot fail to know that the seasons of Heaven and the advantages of Earth depend upon human regulation and control. Our dynasty has methods for famine relief and provisions in storage, and thus has attained the proper way of adapting to the seasons of Heaven; its fields have graded tax rates and its levies are not excessive, and thus it has attained the proper way of adapting to the advantages of Earth. Why then should the price of grain become dear, and why should the dwellings of the people be unsettled by migration? Looking up, I reflect that Your Majesty possesses a heart that cherishes and protects the common people, and has achieved the result of bringing peace to all the myriad states. Yet you still deeply seek ultimate governance, taking the seasons of Heaven and the advantages of Earth to be that upon which the livelihood of the people depends, and therefore wish to regulate and complete them. This especially reveals the vigorous strength of the imperial mind. Your servant begs leave to set this forth for Your Majesty. In recent years, whenever there is a lean harvest, grain becomes scarce and there is nothing with which to supply the people's food; their sacks and pouches are empty and there is nothing with which to sustain the people's livelihood, so that those crying out from hunger and wailing from cold are deeply to be pitied; …

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
民一貧則棄久依之桑梓即新刈之蓬藋而流離播
越者深可憫也米之價既踊則民食且不足尚何望
其出賦稅以充國用民之居既徙則自救且不贍尚
何望其効勤誠以固邦本哉茲不能無廑於
聖慮也為今之計莫若選監臨之官行便宜之政知歲無
常稔而有可常之道必思患預防斂散以時若前代
常平之法斯可行也擇守令之賢行子惠之政知民
有常懷而遂其有常之情必量地分田因民制產若
前代均田之制庶可為也盖常平之法兆於齊魏而
成於耿壽昌均田之制行於後魏而出於李安世豐
===
則增價糴之以利農凶則減價糶之以利民是之謂
常平男子四十畝婦女二十畝戶絕者以為公田刺
史十五頃縣令以上六頃其田則更代相付是之謂
均田斟酌其宜使合於人情庶豐歉之相濟損益其
制使宜於土俗庶貧富之適均綏輯之道豈要於此
乎然究其本則在於
陛下是心之誠而已誠心以為之而必期其效則天下莫
不席於飽食煖衣之域民生莫不囿於安居樂業之
中尚何慮其有失所者哉夫內資文治外資武功文
臣武將之並用威勢德化之並行乃久安長治之計

punctuated:
民一貧則棄久依之桑梓，即新刈之蓬藋，而流離播越者深可憫也。米之價既踊，則民食且不足，尚何望其出賦稅以充國用？民之居既徙，則自救且不贍，尚何望其効勤誠以固邦本哉？茲不能無廑於聖慮也。為今之計，莫若選監臨之官，行便宜之政，知歲無常稔而有可常之道，必思患預防，斂散以時，若前代常平之法，斯可行也；擇守令之賢，行子惠之政，知民有常懷而遂其有常之情，必量地分田，因民制產，若前代均田之制，庶可為也。盖常平之法，兆於齊、魏而成於耿壽昌；均田之制，行於後魏而出於李安世。豐則增價糴之以利農，凶則減價糶之以利民，是之謂常平；男子四十畝，婦女二十畝，戶絕者以為公田，刺史十五頃，縣令以上六頃，其田則更代相付，是之謂均田。斟酌其宜，使合於人情，庶豐歉之相濟；損益其制，使宜於土俗，庶貧富之適均。綏輯之道，豈要於此乎？然究其本，則在於陛下是心之誠而已。誠心以為之，而必期其效，則天下莫不席於飽食煖衣之域，民生莫不囿於安居樂業之中，尚何慮其有失所者哉！

夫內資文治，外資武功，文臣武將之並用，威勢德化之並行，乃久安長治之計…
translation_en:
Once the people fall into poverty, they abandon the native homes they have long relied upon and betake themselves to newly cleared patches of weeds and brushwood; those who wander in destitution and displacement are deeply to be pitied. When the price of rice surges, the people do not even have enough food—how then can one hope for them to pay taxes to supply the needs of the state? When the people's dwellings are uprooted, they cannot even manage to save themselves—how then can one hope for them to exert diligent devotion to strengthen the foundation of the realm? This cannot fail to weigh upon Your Sacred Thought.

As a plan for the present, nothing would be better than to select supervising officials to carry out expedient measures: knowing that harvests are not always abundant yet there is a constant way to prepare for them, they must anticipate disasters and guard against them in advance, gathering and disbursing grain according to the season—thus something like the Ever-Normal Granary system (changping zhi fa) of former dynasties can be put into practice. And one should choose worthy Prefects and Magistrates to carry out paternal and benevolent governance: knowing that the people have constant attachments and fulfilling their constant sentiments, they must measure the land to apportion fields and regulate property according to the population—thus something like the Equal-Field system (juntian zhi zhi) of former dynasties may perhaps be enacted.

Indeed, the Ever-Normal Granary system began in Qi and Wei and was brought to completion by Geng Shouchang; the Equal-Field system was practiced in the Later Wei and originated with Li Anshi. In years of abundance, buying up grain at an increased price in order to benefit the farmers, and in years of dearth, selling off grain at a reduced price in order to benefit the people—this is what is called the Ever-Normal Granary. Allotting forty mu to a man and twenty mu to a woman, making the land of extinguished households into public fields, and granting fifteen qing to a Regional Inspector (cishi) and six qing to officials of the rank of District Magistrate (xianling) and above, with those fields handed over from one incumbent to the next upon replacement—this is what is called the Equal-Field system. If we deliberate on what is appropriate so as to bring it into harmony with human sentiment, then years of plenty and dearth may mutually relieve one another; if we trim or augment the institution so as to suit local customs, then wealth and poverty may be properly equalized. Could there be anything more essential than this in the way of pacifying and gathering the people? Yet if we trace it to its root, it lies simply in the sincerity of this mind of Your Majesty. If You carry it out with a sincere mind and unfailingly insist upon its efficacy, then all under Heaven will without exception rest within the realm of full stomachs and warm clothing, and the people's livelihood will without exception be encompassed within peaceful dwellings and joyful occupations—what worry would there still be that anyone might lose his place!

Now, relying internally on civil governance and externally on military achievement, employing civil officials and military commanders side by side, and practicing awe-inspiring authority and virtuous transformation together—this is the plan for long-term peace and enduring order…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:

死舉無所憾實參贊燮理之功也若乃致治大道必
有至言古之臣獻言於君雖有可采而不能無弊若

言得聖道之經也鼂錯上言兵事思慮周密尊君抑

經然陰陽災異之言未免流於迂而不切鼂錯雖得
聖道之權然刑名術數之論未免流於詐而不正故

punctuated:
也；上因天時，下因地利，安老懷少皆有所資，養生喪死舉無所憾，實參贊燮理之功也。
若乃致治大道，必有至言。古之臣獻言於君，雖有可采，而不能無弊。若董仲舒道明三代，學貫天人，議論淵源，理義醞藉，其言得聖道之經也；鼂錯上言兵事，思慮周密，尊君抑臣，辭氣激烈，其論得聖道之權也。仲舒雖得聖道之經，然陰陽災異之言未免流於迂而不切；鼂錯雖得聖道之權，然刑名術數之論未免流於詐而不正。故宋儒蘇洵因論賈誼而言二子，盖得其當矣。賈誼以年少之資而被孝文之召，觀其《治安》一策，有忠愛之至誠，勸興禮樂，知教化之先務，其辭辯矣；張良以豪傑之才而輔高帝之興，運籌決策而定天下之大亂，因事納忠而關天下之大計，其智周矣。賈誼之論雖辯，然草具儀禮，三表五餌，而其術則不密焉；張良之計雖智，然術本權謀，學宗黃老，而其文則不及焉。故宋儒蘇軾因論陸贄而及二臣，盖近乎是矣。
文德也，武功也，救荒也，安民也，此四者之務固所當講；仲舒也，鼂錯也，賈誼也，張良也，此四臣之偏亦所當知。大抵文武之選不必拘也，在乎可以行於今；安養之道不必泥也，在乎有以利於民。使得人以司文武之選，
translation_en:
… [for enduring peace and lasting governance]; above, conforming to the seasons of Heaven, and below, taking advantage of the benefits of the earth, so that comforting the aged and cherishing the young both have the resources they need, and nourishing the living and burying the dead leave nothing to regret—this is truly the achievement of participating in cosmic transformation and harmonizing the realm.

As for the great Way of bringing about order, there must be consummate words. When ministers of antiquity presented words to their rulers, although there was much worth adopting, they could not be without flaws. For instance, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 illuminated the Way of the Three Dynasties and his learning penetrated Heaven and humanity; his discussions were deep in origin and his moral principles were rich and cultivated—his words grasped the constant standard (jing 經) of the Sage's Way. Chao Cuo 鼂錯 submitted memorials on military affairs with comprehensive and meticulous forethought; in exalting the ruler and restraining the ministers, his diction and spirit were fierce and vehement—his arguments grasped the expedient adaptation (quan 權) of the Sage's Way. Yet although Zhongshu grasped the constant standard of the Sage's Way, his talk of yin-yang and portents of disaster could not avoid sliding into pedantry and impracticality; and although Chao Cuo grasped the expedient adaptation of the Sage's Way, his arguments on administrative accountability (xingming 刑名) and statecraft techniques (shushu 術數) could not avoid sliding into deceit and impropriety. Therefore, when the Song Confucian Su Xun 蘇洵, in the course of discussing Jia Yi 賈誼, spoke of these two men, he hit the mark. Jia Yi, with the endowments of youth, was summoned by Emperor Xiaowen 孝文; looking at his single policy essay on "Securing Peace and Order" (Zhi'an ce 治安策), it possessed the utmost sincerity of loyal affection, urged the promotion of rites and music, and understood the foremost task of moral transformation—his rhetoric was eloquent indeed. Zhang Liang 張良, with the talent of a hero, assisted in the rise of Emperor Gaozu 高帝; devising strategies and deciding policies, he settled the great disorder of the empire, and seizing upon events to offer loyal counsel, he addressed the great plans of the realm—his wisdom was comprehensive indeed. Yet although Jia Yi's arguments were eloquent, in drafting ceremonial protocols and proposing the "three demonstrations and five baits" (sanbiao wu'er 三表五餌), his methods lacked rigor; and although Zhang Liang's plans were wise, his techniques were rooted in tactical machinations and his learning took Huang-Lao 黃老 as its authority, so his literary and moral culture fell short. Therefore, when the Song Confucian Su Shi 蘇軾, in the course of discussing Lu Zhi 陸贄, touched upon these two ministers, he came close to the truth.

Civil virtue, martial merit, famine relief, and pacifying the people—these four tasks are assuredly what ought to be studied. Zhongshu, Chao Cuo, Jia Yi, and Zhang Liang—the biases of these four ministers are also what ought to be known. On the whole, the selection of civil and military officials need not be rigidly bound by precedent; what matters is that it can be put into practice today. The way of pacifying and nourishing the people need not be stubbornly inflexible; what matters is that it brings benefit to the people. If we obtain the right men to take charge of the selection of civil and military officials…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄

而能隨勢以變通得人以主安養之道而能度時以
舉行則品節適中而宜於時矣仲舒賈誼之失由乎

陛下獻者良以誠之為道真實無妄純粹無偽徹上徹下

望

punctuated: 而能隨勢以變通，得人以主安養之道，而能度時以舉行，則品節適中而宜於時矣。仲舒、賈誼之失，由乎學術之未精；鼂錯、張良之失，由乎學術之不正。使其泝義理之淵源，而不安於小成，務聖賢之正學，而不雜於他岐，則損過就中而合于道矣。然宜於時、合于道，皆其用之見於外焉爾。苟不本諸誠，則內之體不立，施之必有所不當，行之必至於易倦。故臣終始以誠為陛下獻者，良以誠之為道，真實無妄，純粹無偽，徹上徹下，皆實理之所為，一有所雜則妄矣；悠久不息，周流不已，亘古亘今，皆實心之所為，一有所間則息矣。臣伏望陛下存此誠於雷聲淵默之時，體此誠於酬酢應變之際。凡一念之動，則曰：「吾之念慮，得無有所雜乎？」明以察之，使無一念之或妄；一事之行，則曰：「吾之施為，得無有所間乎？」剛以制之，使無一事之不實，則治道之本立矣。然而一心之微，攻之者眾，或以聲色，或以貨利，或以遊田，或以逸豫。數者一或不審，則欲動於中，而此誠變矣。臣願陛下遠聲色而不邇，厭貨利而不殖，謹遊田而不恣，戒逸
translation_en: …and can adapt flexibly according to the circumstances, and if one obtains the right people to preside over the way of pacifying and nourishing the populace and can assess the times to put it into practice, then the regulations and measures will hit the due mean and be suited to the times. The shortcomings of Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 and Jia Yi 賈誼 stemmed from their scholarship not yet being refined; the shortcomings of Chao Cuo 鼂錯 and Zhang Liang 張良 stemmed from their scholarship not being orthodox. Had they traced the fountainhead of moral principles without resting content in minor achievements, and devoted themselves to the orthodox learning of the sages and worthies without mixing in divergent paths, they would have pared away excess to reach the mean and conformed to the Way. Yet being suited to the times and conforming to the Way are both merely functions manifested on the outside. If they are not rooted in sincerity, the inner substance is not established; when applied, there will surely be things that are inappropriate, and when practiced, it will surely lead to easy fatigue. Therefore, the reason your servant from beginning to end offers "sincerity" to Your Majesty is truly because sincerity as a Way is real and without falsehood, pure and without artifice; penetrating above and below, it is entirely the work of real principle—the moment there is any admixture, it becomes false. Enduring and unceasing, circulating without end, spanning from antiquity to the present, it is entirely the work of a real mind—the moment there is any interruption, it ceases. Your servant humbly hopes that Your Majesty will preserve this sincerity in times of thunderous voice or abyssal silence, and embody this sincerity on occasions of responding to affairs and adapting to changes. Whenever a single thought stirs, say to yourself: "Could there be any admixture in my thoughts and deliberations?" Examine it with clarity, so that not a single thought is ever false. Whenever a single affair is carried out, say to yourself: "Could there be any interruption in my actions and measures?" Regulate it with firmness, so that not a single affair is ever unreal. Thus, the foundation of the way of governance will be established. Nevertheless, subtle as the single mind is, those who assail it are many: some through sensual pleasures of music and beauty, some through goods and profit, some through excursions and hunting, and some through ease and comfort. If there is the slightest lack of scrutiny regarding these several things, desires will stir within, and this sincerity will be altered. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty will keep sensual pleasures at a distance and not approach them, spurn goods and profit and not amass them, be prudent in excursions and hunting and not indulge in them, guard against ease…

泯矣臣願
陛下禁沉湎而弗為戒奢侈而弗行斥異端而弗尚拒諂
諛而弗親不東以西不南以此然後方寸明白久暫

陛下之策臣者臣既已槩陳之而要其歸在乎一誠矣然

君之心不能自己也夫誠固為治道之本而所以行是誠
者又在乎
陛下之明與剛明則有以識其誠之正剛則有以決其誠
之幾明非煩苛伺察之謂乃知道誼識安危別賢愚

punctuated: 豫而不肆，勿貳以二，勿參以三，然後本源澄澈，終始惟一，而此誠豈有間斷哉？或於沉湎，或於奢侈，或於異端，或於諂諛，數者一或不察，則心逐於外而此誠泯矣。臣願陛下禁沉湎而弗為，戒奢侈而弗行，斥異端而弗尚，拒諂諛而弗親，不東以西，不南以此，然後方寸明白，久暫有常，而此誠豈有止息哉？由是可以措民物於熈皞，綿宗社於隆長，重華之德、丕承之功，豈獨專美於舜、武哉！陛下之策臣者，臣既已槩陳之，而要其歸在乎一誠矣。然於終篇復有所獻焉者，蓋愛君之心不能自己也。夫誠固為治道之本，而所以行是誠者，又在乎陛下之明與剛。明則有以識其誠之正，剛則有以決其誠之幾。明非煩苛伺察之謂，乃知道誼、識安危、別賢愚、辯是非之謂也；剛非强亢暴戾之謂，乃惟道所在，斷之不疑，奸不能惑，佞不能移之謂也。陛下誠廓日月之明，無微不察，無幽不燭，如《書》所謂「憲天聰明」；奮乾剛之斷，見義必為，聞善即行，如《書》所謂「惟克果斷」。夫
translation_en:
… against idleness and comfort and not indulge in them; do not let your mind be divided by two things or confounded by three. Only then will the primal source be limpid and clear, remaining constant from beginning to end—and how could this sincerity ever be interrupted? Whether through overindulgence in drink, or through extravagance, or through heterodoxy, or through flattery and sycophancy—if even one of these several things is not examined, the mind will chase after external things and this sincerity will be extinguished. Your servant wishes Your Majesty to prohibit overindulgence in drink and not engage in it, to guard against extravagance and not practice it, to reject heterodoxy and not esteem it, and to repel flattery and sycophancy and not be intimate with them; do not waver between east and west, or between south and north [?]. Only then will your mind be clear and bright, remaining constant through both long and short durations—and how could this sincerity ever cease? From this, you can place the people and all things in a state of harmonious prosperity and extend the ancestral altars in flourishing longevity; how could the virtue of "Double Splendor" and the achievement of "Greatly Continuing" remain the exclusive glory of Shun and King Wu alone!

As for the policy questions Your Majesty has asked your servant, your servant has already set forth a general account of them, and their essential conclusion lies in a single sincerity. Yet at the end of this essay, the reason I again have something to offer is that a heart that loves its ruler cannot stop itself. Now, sincerity is assuredly the foundation of the way of governance, yet that by which this sincerity is put into practice lies further in Your Majesty's clarity of insight and firmness. With clarity of insight, one has the means to recognize the correctness of that sincerity; with firmness, one has the means to decide upon the subtle springs of action of that sincerity. Clarity of insight does not mean vexatious harshness and prying surveillance; rather, it means knowing moral principle and righteousness, recognizing security and danger, distinguishing the worthy from the foolish, and discerning right from wrong. Firmness does not mean overbearing arrogance and violent perversity; rather, it means deciding without doubt wherever the Way resides, so that the wicked cannot delude and theglib cannot sway you. If Your Majesty truly expands a clarity of insight like that of the sun and moon, leaving nothing minute unexamined and nothing obscure unilluminated, just as the Book of Documents (Shu) says, "taking Heaven's聡明 (hearing and sight / intelligence) as a model"; and rouses the decisiveness of Heavenly firmness, never failing to act when seeing what is righteous and immediately practicing what is good upon hearing it, just as the Book of Documents says, "only by being able to be resolute and decisive"—now…

translation_en: … If it is thus, then this sincerity will pervade both inside and outside, and this sincerity will endure from beginning to end. As the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) states, "Utmost sincerity is ceaseless. Being ceaseless, it is lasting. Being lasting, it is manifest. Being manifest, it reaches far and long. Reaching far and long, it becomes broad and thick. Being broad and thick, it becomes high and bright." Thus, nothing of the Way of governing All-under-Heaven will remain unfulfilled. These words of your servant are迂闊 [impractical] and shallow, and indeed seem to hold nothing worthy of adoption; yet they truly stem from a single thought of earnest loyalty. I humbly hope Your Majesty will condescend to cast Your sagely gaze upon them. Then not only would this foolish servant be most fortunate, but All-under-Heaven would truly be most fortunate, and ten thousand generations would be most fortunate. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
臣丁溥
臣對臣聞帝王圖治之道本於心帝王存心之道本
於敬夫敬以存心則心體光明而正大自有以洞察
天下之事機心以圖治則治道平康而正直自有以
克成天下之事業故有志於帝王之圖治者不可不
存其心有志於帝王之存心者不可不盡其敬以此
心之敬理當世之務則疏通文武之選典綏輯天下
之民生無往而不宜於時以此心之敬察昔人之偏
則經權迂詐之得失辯智文術之是非無一而不合
於道尚何患乎文臣武士之壅遏天時地利之凶歉
===
而治道有不陋漢儒之言以比隆唐虞三代之盛哉
欽惟
皇帝陛下稟聰明睿智之資備剛健中正之德即位以來
圖惟治理聲色貨利無所邇殖宮室苑囿無所增廣
布公道以肅紀綱凜乎雷霆之發𦦨獎直言以勵氣
節浩乎江海之納川是以倫紀粲乎其脩明風俗藹
乎其丕變
功業文章巍然煥然而大哉帝堯君哉帝舜不得專美
於前矣然猶
體道謙冲不自滿假

體道謙沖不自滿假
punctuated:
臣丁溥。

臣對：臣聞帝王圖治之道本於心，帝王存心之道本於敬。夫敬以存心，則心體光明而正大，自有以洞察天下之事機；心以圖治，則治道平康而正直，自有以克成天下之事業。故有志於帝王之圖治者，不可不存其心；有志於帝王之存心者，不可不盡其敬。以此心之敬理當世之務，則疏通文武之選典、綏輯天下之民生，無往而不宜於時；以此心之敬察昔人之偏，則經權迂詐之得失、辯智文術之是非，無一而不合於道。尚何患乎文臣武士之壅遏、天時地利之凶歉，而治道有不陋漢儒之言，以比隆唐、虞、三代之盛哉？

欽惟皇帝陛下，稟聰明睿智之資，備剛健中正之德，即位以來，圖惟治理，聲色貨利無所邇殖，宮室苑囿無所增廣；布公道以肅紀綱，凜乎雷霆之發𦦨；獎直言以勵氣節，浩乎江海之納川。是以倫紀粲乎其脩明，風俗藹乎其丕變，功業文章巍然煥然，而「大哉帝堯，君哉帝舜」不得專美於前矣。然猶體道謙冲，不自滿假，
translation_en:
Your servant Ding Pu 丁溥.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the way by which emperors and kings plan for governance is rooted in the mind, and the way by which emperors and kings preserve their minds is rooted in reverence. Indeed, when one preserves the mind with reverence, the substance of the mind is luminous, upright, and great, naturally enabling one to penetrate the critical workings of affairs throughout the realm; when one plans for governance with the mind, the way of governance is peaceful, tranquil, and upright, naturally enabling one to accomplish the great enterprises of the realm. Therefore, one who aspires to the governance planned by emperors and kings cannot fail to preserve his mind; and one who aspires to the preservation of the mind practiced by emperors and kings cannot fail to exhaust his reverence. If, with the reverence of this mind, one orders the affairs of the present age, then in clearing the selection statutes for civil and military officials and pacifying and comforting the livelihood of the people of the realm, there will be nothing that is not suited to the times; if, with the reverence of this mind, one examines the biases of men of the past, then in judging the merits and demerits of standard principles versus expediency, or pedantry versus deceit, and the right and wrong of eloquence and cleverness versus literary cultivation and statecraft, there will not be a single thing that does not conform to the Way. What worry, then, would there still be over the obstruction of civil officials and military officers, or over bad harvests and dearth arising from the seasons of heaven and the advantages of the earth? And how could the way of governance fail to look down upon the words of the Han Confucians as shallow, and rival in splendor the flourishing ages of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties?

Reverently, I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed with a nature of keen intelligence and sagely wisdom, and possesses the virtues of firm strength and central uprightness. Since ascending the throne, You have planned solely for good governance: sensual pleasures and material wealth You have neither approached nor accumulated; palaces and hunting parks You have not expanded. You have promulgated public justice to make stringent the laws and institutions, awe-inspiring as the flash and blaze of thunderbolts; You have encouraged forthright speech to rouse moral integrity, vast as the great rivers and seas receiving the streams. Thus human relations and moral norms are brilliantly cultivated and clarified, customs are harmoniously and greatly transformed, and Your achievements and cultural splendor are lofty and resplendent—so that those praised with the words "Great indeed was Sovereign Yao!" and "A true ruler indeed was Sovereign Shun!" cannot monopolize beauty in antiquity. Yet even so, You embody the Way in modest humility, not allowing Yourself to become self-satisfied or complacent, …

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
廷集多士咨訪治道拳拳以治功弗張為言孜孜以政
績罕著為慮臣有以知
陛下念
祖宗創業之艱難思今日守成之不易志在康乂兆民保安
社稷夙夜靡寧真堯舜之用心也顧臣淺陋曷克以仰承
聖詔茂明大對以裨治道之萬一耶伏觀
太祖高皇帝
太宗文皇帝順天人之心以建不拔之業其治世求言之
道垂裕後昆而無間
仁宗昭皇帝
===
===
宣宗章皇帝
英宗睿皇帝協天人之心以綿無窮之祚其治世求言之
道仰紹前烈而有光
皇明誕啓曆數無疆
陛下今日所受之天命即
祖宗列聖之所昭受者臣願
陛下以天心為心常存敬天之實則乘六龍以御天尊
居九重以凝命福祿與
陛下萬年而安享此非臣之諛言也周公告成王嘗曰永
言配命自求多福寧無故哉

punctuated: 廷集多士，咨訪治道，拳拳以治功弗張為言，孜孜以政績罕著為慮。臣有以知陛下念祖宗創業之艱難，思今日守成之不易，志在康乂兆民，保安社稷，夙夜靡寧，真堯、舜之用心也。顧臣淺陋，曷克以仰承聖詔，茂明大對，以裨治道之萬一耶？伏觀太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝，順天人之心，以建不拔之業，其治世求言之道，垂裕後昆而無間；仁宗昭皇帝、宣宗章皇帝、英宗睿皇帝，協天人之心，以綿無窮之祚，其治世求言之道，仰紹前烈而有光。皇明誕啓，曆數無疆。陛下今日所受之天命，即祖宗列聖之所昭受者。臣願陛下以天心為心，常存敬天之實，則乘六龍以御天，尊居九重以凝命，福祿與陛下萬年而安享。此非臣之諛言也，周公告成王嘗曰：「永言配命，自求多福。」寧無故哉？
translation_en:
…gather the many scholars in the palace court to inquire into the Way of governance, earnestly speaking of how the achievements of rule have not yet been fully extended, and tirelessly worrying that administrative accomplishments are rarely manifest. By this your servant knows that Your Majesty remembers the hardships of the Imperial Ancestors in founding the dynasty, reflects on the difficulty of preserving their accomplishments today, and sets Your mind on bringing peace and order to the millions of people and securing the altars of state—never resting day or night. Truly, this is the very mind of Yao and Shun! Yet given how shallow and rustic your servant is, how could I be capable of worthily receiving Your Sacred Edict and brilliantly expounding a grand reply so as to contribute even one ten-thousandth to the Way of governance?

Humbly I observe that Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu) and Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen (Taizong) accorded with the hearts of Heaven and humanity to establish an unshakeable enterprise; their Way of governing the world and seeking frank counsel has bequeathed abundance to posterity without interruption. Benevolent Ancestor Emperor Zhao (Renzong), Proclaiming Ancestor Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong), and Heroic Ancestor Emperor Rui (Yingzong) harmonized the hearts of Heaven and humanity to prolong a boundless dynastic fortune; their Way of governing the world and seeking frank counsel looked up to continue the illustrious achievements of their predecessors and added luster to them. The August Ming has grandly opened its destiny, and its ordained years are without limit.

The Mandate of Heaven that Your Majesty receives today is the very same that the Imperial Ancestors and successive Sacred Emperors brightly received. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty take the mind of Heaven as Your own mind and always preserve the reality of revering Heaven; then You shall mount the six dragons to drive across the sky, dwell in exalted dignity within the ninefold palace enclosures to consolidate the Mandate, and good fortune and blessings shall be peacefully enjoyed by Your Majesty for ten thousand years. These are not flattering words from your servant: when the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng, he once said, "Forever strive to match the Mandate, and thereby seek much blessing for yourself." Could this have been said without reason?

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
陛下今日所孚之人心即
祖宗列聖之所素孚者臣願
陛下以民心為心恒切勤民之念則車書會同於四海玉
帛來王於萬國邦家賴
陛下萬年而鞏固此非臣之迂談也召公告成王嘗曰豈
弟君子民之父母寧無自哉伊欲盡天人之責其要
在於簡文臣而精武選盖文有科第胄監之差有賢
良才德之別擇其材之深於文者或識達治體或通
曉世故所以理民事也武有親貴勲勞之異有行伍
卒隸之殊拔其功之優於武者或智略精銳或弓馬
===
熟閑所以馭兵戎也我
國家內資乎文外資乎武文武內外維持一德與武王
保有厥士克定厥家同符而合轍矣奈何典銓選者
惟知體
陛下寬厚之仁不務嚴黜陟之法故竊名文學者或壞科
目以進身或肆貪墨以苟祿則銓衡之途烏得而不
壅昧諳韜略者或循資蔭以承襲或冒功次以超越
則衛所之員烏得而不溢是誠有以勦
聖志之所慮矣誠深省之薰蕕無別涇渭不分惡在其能
疏通也哉臣願

熟閑所以馭兵戎也我
國家内資乎文外資乎武文武内外維持一德與武王
保有厥士克定厥家同符而合轍矣柰何典銓選者
惟知體
陛下寛厚之仁不務嚴黜陟之法故竊名文學者或壞科
目以進身或肆貪墨以苟祿則銓衡之途烏得而不
壅昧韜略者或循資蔭以承襲或冐功次以超越
則衛所之員烏得而不濫是誠有以勤
聖志之所慮矣試深省之薰蕕無别涇渭不分惡在其能
號遷也哉臣願
punctuated:
陛下今日所孚之人心，即祖宗列聖之所素孚者。臣願陛下以民心為心，恒切勤民之念，則車書會同於四海，玉帛來王於萬國，邦家賴陛下萬年而鞏固。此非臣之迂談也，召公告成王嘗曰：「豈弟君子，民之父母。」寧無自哉！

伊欲盡天人之責，其要在於簡文臣而精武選。盖文有科第、胄監之差，有賢良、才德之別，擇其材之深於文者，或識達治體，或通曉世故，所以理民事也；武有親貴、勲勞之異，有行伍、卒隸之殊，拔其功之優於武者，或智略精銳，或弓馬熟閑，所以馭兵戎也。我國家內資乎文，外資乎武，文武內外，維持一德，與武王「保有厥士，克定厥家」同符而合轍矣。奈何典銓選者，惟知體陛下寬厚之仁，不務嚴黜陟之法，故竊名文學者，或壞科目以進身，或肆貪墨以苟祿，則銓衡之途烏得而不壅？昧諳韜略者，或循資蔭以承襲，或冒功次以超越，則衛所之員烏得而不溢？是誠有以勦聖志之所慮矣。誠深省之，薰蕕無別，涇渭不分，惡在其能疏通也哉！臣願
translation_en:
The hearts of the people in which Your Majesty commands trust today are the very ones in which the Imperial Ancestors and successive sage emperors long commanded trust. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty take the heart of the common people as your own heart and constantly cherish an earnest concern for toiling on behalf of the people; then carriage gauges and writing systems will be unified throughout the Four Seas, jade and silk will be brought in homage from the myriad states, and the state and dynasty will rely on Your Majesty to remain securely consolidated for ten thousand years. This is not pedantic talk on your servant's part. When the Duke of Shao admonished King Cheng, he once said: "Easy and fraternal is the lord, father and mother of the people." Could this have been without a source?

Now, if one wishes to fulfill the responsibilities toward Heaven and humanity, the essential point lies in carefully selecting civil officials and refining military appointments. For in the civil service, there are distinctions between examination graduates and students of the Directorate of Education, and differentiations among the worthy and good, the talented and virtuous. Selecting those whose abilities are profound in civil affairs—whether their insight reaches to the fundamentals of governance or they thoroughly understand the ways of the world—is the means by which civil affairs are ordered. In the military service, there are differences between imperial relatives and nobles and those of meritorious service, and distinctions among the ranks and common soldiers. Promoting those whose achievements excel in military affairs—whether they are sharp in strategic intelligence or skilled and practiced in archery and horsemanship—is the means by which armed forces are commanded. Our dynasty relies internally on the civil and externally on the military; civil and military, inside and out, uphold a single virtue, tallying and sharing the same track with King Wu's "preserving his officers and thereby stabilizing his house." How is it, then, that those in charge of personnel selection only know how to embody Your Majesty's寬厚 (generous and benevolent) kindness, without striving to strictly enforce the laws of demotion and promotion? Consequently, those who usurp a reputation for literary learning either corrupt the examination categories to advance themselves or indulge in greed and venality to illicitly draw a salary—how then could the path of civil selection fail to become clogged? Those who are ignorant of military strategy either follow seniority and hereditary privilege to succeed to posts or falsely claim grades of merit to leapfrog in rank—how then could the personnel in the Guards and Battalions fail to become excessive? This truly gives cause to weary the concerns of Your Sacred Mind. If one examines this deeply, when fragrant herbs and foul weeds are not distinguished, and the clear Wei and muddy Jing rivers are not separated, how can the channels possibly be cleared and opened? Your servant wishes that…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
陛下攬乾綱於獨斷揭日月於中天戒令大臣恪遵成憲
嚴加考覈濫舉有禁犯者不能緩其刑倖進有罰来
者不容踵其迹有上粮馬而入監聽選者杜僥倖於
将来有擁貔貅而坐食妨政者汰浮冗於既往庸愚
不得以叨爵祿老弱不得以占名器曾不聞昔人名
利虛實之說乎職事一官以序才能以位賢德施實
利而寓之虛名勳爵散號以馭崇貴以甄功勞假虛
名而佐其實利疏通之道端不出此矣伊欲契天人
之心其要在於足民食而奠民居盖陰陽愆伏水旱
流行而為灾為虐此歲無常稔者天之道也鄉田同

陛下攬乾綱於獨斷，揭日月於中天，戒令大臣恪遵成憲，嚴加考覈。濫舉有禁，犯者不能緩其刑；倖進有罰，来者不容踵其迹。有上粮馬而入監聽選者，杜僥倖於将来；有擁貔貅而坐食妨政者，汰浮冗於既往。庸愚不得以叨爵祿，老弱不得以占名器。曾不聞昔人名利虛實之說乎？職事一官，以序才能、以位賢德，施實利而寓之虛名；勳爵散號，以馭崇貴、以甄功勞，假虛名而佐其實利。疏通之道，端不出此矣。

伊欲契天人之心，其要在於足民食而奠民居。盖陰陽愆伏，水旱流行，而為灾為虐，此歲無常稔者，天之道也；鄉田同井，出入守望，而相友相助，此土有常懷者，人之情也。我國家上安乎天，下安乎人，天人上下，感通一理，與文王「燕及皇天，克昌厥後」同條而共貫矣。奈何職司牧者，罔念行陛下寬恤之政，惟欲峻掊克之私。故旱乾水溢之靡常，而年穀不登，何免貴糴以充餒？仰事俯育之無賴，而貧乏不堪，何免離散以苟全？是真有以勞聖心之所憂矣。請詳究之：歛散無方，田制不定，惡在其能綏輯也哉？臣願
translation_en:
… Your Majesty grasp the sovereign authority in Your sole decision and hold up the sun and moon in mid-heaven, admonishing and commanding the great ministers to respectfully abide by the established constitutions and strictly conduct evaluations and verifications. For reckless recommendations there should be prohibitions, so that offenders cannot delay their punishment; for opportunistic advancement there should be penalties, so that newcomers are not permitted to follow in their footsteps. As for those who contribute grain and horses to enter the Directorate of Education and await selection, block such opportunism for the future; as for those who command brave troops yet sit idle, eating without working and hindering governance, weed out such superfluous redundancies from the past. The mediocre and foolish will not be able to unworthily enjoy noble ranks and emoluments, and the old and weak will not be able to occupy official titles and insignia. Have You not heard the saying of men of old regarding the emptiness and substance of titles and benefits? Functional offices, which rank talent and ability and place the worthy and virtuous, confer substantive benefits while investing them with nominal titles; merit titles, titles of nobility, and prestige titles, which govern the exalted and noble and distinguish meritorious service, borrow nominal titles to assist substantive benefits. The way to clear congestion truly does not go beyond this.

If one wishes to accord with the minds of Heaven and humankind, the essential point lies in making the people's food sufficient and settling the people's dwellings. For yin and yang err and stagnate, floods and droughts spread abroad, bringing disaster and wreaking havoc—that the harvests are not constantly abundant is the way of Heaven. Those of the same district and fields share a well-system, keeping watch on going out and coming in, befriending and helping one another—that they constantly cherish their native soil is the sentiment of humankind. Our Dynasty above brings peace to Heaven and below brings peace to humankind; Heaven and humankind, above and below, respond to and penetrate one another through a single principle, sharing the same thread and continuity as King Wen, who "brought peace even unto August Heaven, and was able to make prosperous his descendants." Why is it, then, that those who hold the office of shepherding the people take no thought to carry out Your Majesty's policies of leniency and compassion, desiring only to pursue the selfish severity of extortionate exactions? Thus, when droughts and floods occur irregularly and the annual grain crops fail to ripen, how can the people avoid buying grain at high prices to fill their hungry bellies? When they have nothing to rely upon to serve their parents above and nurture their children below, and their poverty and destitution become unbearable, how can they avoid scattering and fleeing to merely preserve their lives? This truly gives cause to burden the anxieties of Your Sacred Mind. Allow me to examine this in detail: if gathering and dispensing grain lack a proper method, and the system of land tenure is not fixed, how can they possibly pacify and gather the people? Your servant wishes that …

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
陛下揔機務於自裁敷雨露於九有申飭大臣按行有司
頻加督勸遇歲豐歉倉廩皆有實儲臨民出納主典
不敢侵奪有守田廬而貧餒者賑而安之有就耕食
而流亡者招而撫之豪强不得以恣漁獵貪酷不得
以肆徵科獨不觀前代常平均田之事乎穀賤則增
價而糴以利農穀貴則減價而糶以利民雖不逮乎
周官荒政之良而耿壽昌權時之計猶可舉男子婦
人四十畝二十畝皆有等縣令刺史六頃十五頃皆
有則雖不侔乎分田制祿之善而李安世濟時之策
尚可行綏輯之道亦不外此矣夫天下之臣工孰不
===
揔核於文武誠使疏通之道名利相須虛實相濟庶
乎兼資文武有其人矣由是文以附衆足以裕邦計
而内治脩武以威敵足以捍邊陲而外夷攘豈不周
一世之用乎天下之民生孰不根本於天地誠使綏
輯之道常平有法均田有制庶乎財成天地盡其道
矣由是水土奠而民居安天時有以應於上五穀熟
而人民育人事有以協於下豈不遂萬姓之安乎雖
然求大道以圖治必切於時宜資治道於至言當稽
諸往古董生天人三策度越諸子彷彿乎聖道之經
宜適用也其縱陽閉陰之說如迂何晁錯邊事一奏

而人民育人事有以協於下豈不遂萬姓之安乎雖

punctuated:
陛下揔機務於自裁，敷雨露於九有，申飭大臣，按行有司，頻加督勸。遇歲豐歉，倉廩皆有實儲；臨民出納，主典不敢侵奪。有守田廬而貧餒者，賑而安之；有就耕食而流亡者，招而撫之。豪强不得以恣漁獵，貪酷不得以肆徵科。獨不觀前代常平、均田之事乎？穀賤則增價而糴以利農，穀貴則減價而糶以利民，雖不逮乎《周官》荒政之良，而耿壽昌權時之計猶可舉；男子、婦人四十畝、二十畝皆有等，縣令、刺史六頃、十五頃皆有則，雖不侔乎分田制祿之善，而李安世濟時之策尚可行。綏輯之道，亦不外此矣。

夫天下之臣工，孰不揔核於文武？誠使疏通之道，名利相須，虛實相濟，庶乎兼資文武有其人矣。由是文以附衆，足以裕邦計而内治脩；武以威敵，足以捍邊陲而外夷攘，豈不周一世之用乎？天下之民生，孰不根本於天地？誠使綏輯之道，常平有法，均田有制，庶乎財成天地盡其道矣。由是水土奠而民居安，天時有以應於上；五穀熟而人民育，人事有以協於下，豈不遂萬姓之安乎？

雖然，求大道以圖治，必切於時宜；資治道於至言，當稽諸往古。董生天人三策，度越諸子，彷彿乎聖道之經，宜適用也，其縱陽閉陰之說如迂何？晁錯邊事一奏，
translation_en:
…Your Majesty take overall control of state affairs through Your own personal decisions, spread the rain and dew of Your grace across the Nine Regions, strictly instruct the great ministers, and send inspectors to tour the local authorities, frequently overseeing and encouraging them. Whether the harvest is abundant or lean, the granaries will all hold real reserves; when dispensing to or collecting from the people, the clerks in charge will not dare to embezzle or plunder. Those who stay by their fields and huts yet suffer poverty and hunger should be relieved and settled; those who have fled as refugees in search of land to till and food to eat should be summoned back and comforted. The powerful and overbearing must not be allowed to prey on the people at will, nor the greedy and cruel to impose unrestrained exactions and levies. Have You alone not considered the Ever-Normal Granaries and the Equal-Field system of former dynasties? When grain was cheap, the state bought it at an increased price to benefit the farmers; when grain was dear, the state sold it at a reduced price to benefit the people. Although this did not match the excellence of the famine-relief policies in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), Geng Shouchang's expedient plan for the times can still be put into effect. Men and women were allotted forty mu and twenty mu in graded amounts, while District Magistrates and Regional Inspectors were granted six qing and fifteen qing according to fixed rules. Although this did not equal the perfection of ancient land division and emolument regulations, Li Anshi's policy for rescuing the age can still be practiced. The way to pacify and gather the people lies in nothing beyond this.

Now, among all the officials of the realm, who is not comprehensively assessed through civil and military arts? If in the way of opening career paths, reputation and practical benefit complement each other, and nominal rank and actual duty reinforce one another, then we may hope to find men endowed with both civil and military talents. Thereby, using civil administration to win the allegiance of the multitude will suffice to enrich the state's finances and cultivate internal governance; using military might to overawe the enemy will suffice to defend the frontiers and repel foreign barbarians—would this not meet all the needs of a generation? Among the livelihoods of all the people in the realm, which is not rooted in Heaven and Earth? If in the way of pacifying and gathering the people, the Ever-Normal Granaries have their regulations and the Equal-Field system has its institutions, then we may hope to fulfill the way of regulating and completing the work of Heaven and Earth. Thereby, water and soil are settled so the people's dwellings are secure, and the heavenly seasons respond above; the five grains ripen so the populace is nourished, and human affairs harmonize below—would this not achieve peace for the myriad姓 (people)?

Even so, in seeking the Great Way to plan for governance, one must suit the needs of the times; in drawing principles of governance from supreme words, one ought to examine the past. Master Dong's [Dong Zhongshu's] three policy essays on Heaven and humanity surpassed those of all other masters and closely resembled the constant principles of the Sage's Way, so they ought to be applicable in practice—yet what of the impracticality of his theory of releasing yang and shutting off yin? Chao Cuo's memorial on frontier affairs…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
璽書褒美依於聖道之權似濟時也其刑名術數
之學如詐何𨒫宋儒蘇洵之論其得失胥可知矣文
帝武帝以直言策士而所言未必皆直較之言合稷
契謂之忠者為何如治安一書通達國體辯莫辯於
賈誼矣而五餌三表以係單于之屬術果密於陸贄
乎運籌决勝躡足附耳智莫智於張良矣而學宗黃
老以從赤松之遊文果及於陸贄乎觀宋儒蘇軾之
論其是非互可見矣高帝文帝以正議求士而所議
未必皆正揆之謨合皐陶謂之嘉者為何若噫此漢
之君臣所以不唐虞三代之君臣而漢之治功所以
===
不唐虞三代之治功以自汩沒於雜霸深可為之太
息者抑通論之豈惟漢哉前乎漢也縱橫於戰國棄
滅於嬴秦唐虞三代之禮樂教化何寥寥乎後乎漢
也夷風雜於唐道不純於宋唐虞三代之聲名文物
何落落乎天運循環無往不復洪惟
天朝
列聖繼作謠康衢於春臺玉燭之中歌明良於景星慶雲
之下肆惟
皇上適際隆興以不世出之才當大有為之日遠宗唐虞
三代之道近守

punctuated: 璽書褒美，依於聖道之權，似濟時也，其刑名術數之學，如詐何？𨒫宋儒蘇洵之論，其得失胥可知矣。文帝、武帝以直言策士，而所言未必皆直，較之「言合稷契謂之忠」者，為何如？治安一書，通達國體，辯莫辯於賈誼矣，而五餌三表以係單于之屬，術果密於陸贄乎？運籌决勝，躡足附耳，智莫智於張良矣，而學宗黃老以從赤松之遊，文果及於陸贄乎？觀宋儒蘇軾之論，其是非互可見矣。高帝、文帝以正議求士，而所議未必皆正，揆之「謨合皐陶謂之嘉」者，為何若？噫！此漢之君臣所以不唐虞三代之君臣，而漢之治功所以不唐虞三代之治功，以自汩沒於雜霸，深可為之太息者。抑通論之，豈惟漢哉？前乎漢也，縱橫於戰國，棄滅於嬴秦，唐虞三代之禮樂教化何寥寥乎！後乎漢也，夷風雜於唐，道不純於宋，唐虞三代之聲名文物何落落乎！天運循環，無往不復。洪惟天朝，列聖繼作，謠康衢於春臺玉燭之中，歌明良於景星慶雲之下。肆惟皇上，適際隆興，以不世出之才，當大有為之日，遠宗唐虞三代之道，近守
translation_en: … was praised in a sealed imperial rescript, and in relying on the expediency of the sagely Way, it seemed suited to assist the times; yet what of its craftiness in the study of penal law and statecraft techniques? Following the discourse of the Song Confucian Su Xun 蘇洵, the merits and failings of both can be known together. Emperor Wen 文帝 and Emperor Wu 武帝 of Han examined scholars on policy questions calling for forthright speech, yet what was spoken was not necessarily all forthright; how does this compare with "speech that accords with Hou Ji 后稷 and Xie 契 is called loyal"? In his single memorial on securing peace and order, Jia Yi 賈誼 thoroughly grasped the fundamentals of the state—no one was more eloquent in argument than he; yet with his "five baits" and "three demonstrations" to bind the Chanyu and his kind, were his stratagems truly more thoroughgoing than those of Lu Zhi 陸贄? In devising strategies that determined victory, stepping on his lord's foot and whispering in his ear, no one was wiser than Zhang Liang 張良; yet in taking Huang-Lao 黃老 as the foundation of his learning and seeking to roam with Master Redpine (Chisongzi 赤松子), did his literary learning truly match that of Lu Zhi? Examining the discourse of the Song Confucian Su Shi 蘇軾, the rights and wrongs of each become mutually apparent. Emperor Gao 高帝 and Emperor Wen sought scholars for their orthodox deliberations, yet what they deliberated was not necessarily all orthodox; how does this measure up to "counsels that accord with Gao Yao 皐陶 are called admirable"? Alas! This is why the rulers and ministers of the Han failed to be like the rulers and ministers of Tang 唐, Yu 虞, and the Three Dynasties, and why the governing achievements of the Han failed to be like the governing achievements of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, sinking themselves instead into an impure霸 (hegemonic) rule—something over which one may deeply sigh! Moreover, if we discuss the matter comprehensively, was this true only of the Han? Before the Han, there were the alliance strategists of the Warring States and the abandonment and destruction wrought by the Ying-clan Qin 嬴秦—how sparse and desolate were the rites, music, and moral transformation of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties! After the Han, barbarian customs were mixed in during the Tang, and the Way was not pure during the宋 (Song)—how scattered and rare were the illustrious renown and cultural institutions of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties! The movement of Heaven revolves in cycles; there is no going forth without a return. Humbly considering our Great Dynasty, a succession of sacred emperors has arisen one after another, singing ballads of the highroads amid the spring terrace and the jade-like harmony of the seasons, and chanting songs of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers beneath auspicious stars and felicitous clouds. And now Your Majesty has met with this era of flourishing resurgence; with talent that appears but once in an age, at a time for great achievements, You venerate from afar the Way of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and closely uphold…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
祖宗列聖之法啓臣以當世四者之務陳之必宜於時諭
臣以前代四臣之偏矯之必合於道臣又以見
陛下知周萬物而不棄於一得之愚明照四方而必詢于
芻蕘之賤意者欲與忠貞之士商論治道權衡人物
以壽億萬年太平之象也臣復為
陛下尋繹其義以推廣其說夫時者當其可之謂不當其
可則非時矣四者之務謂之非時不可也臣以聖賢
救時之心論之曰銓衡途壅曰衛所員濫務明黜陟
之法則可否則賢否混淆而不可曰歉則糴貴曰貧
則民徙務禁掊克之私則可否則天人胥憤而不可
===

陛下奚待他求哉古之禹思天下有溺者由己溺之稷思
天下有飢者由己飢之能法禹稷之心急於救時于
以建官位事發政施仁措斯世於唐虞三代之雍熈
何難耶若使任官惟賢有乖於周官之制捍災禦患
有愧於雲漢之章則非庶務不宜於時所以理之失
其時耳臣故舉此以為緩於救時者之警也道者所
當行之謂所不當行則非道矣四臣之言謂之非道
不可也臣以聖賢行道之心論之曰經曰權有時可
行而或迂或詐之虧於治體則不可行曰辯曰智有

… the laws of the Ancestors and the successive sage emperors, opening Your servant's mind with the four pressing tasks of the present age, which when set forth must be suited to the times, and instructing Your servant regarding the partialities of the four ministers of former dynasties, which when rectified must accord with the Way. From this Your servant further perceives that Your Majesty's wisdom encompasses all things, yet You do not spurn the humble insight of a foolish man; Your brilliance illuminates the four quarters, yet You unfailingly consult even the lowly gatherers of firewood and grass. Surely Your intention is to deliberate upon the Way of governance and weigh men of talent together with loyal and upright scholars, so as to prolong the manifestations of supreme peace for hundreds of millions of years. Your servant shall again unravel the meaning of these matters for Your Majesty in order to expand upon their explanation.

Now, "timeliness" means seizing what is appropriate to the moment; if it does not match what is appropriate, then it is untimely. As for the four pressing tasks, one cannot say they are untimely. If Your servant discusses them from the standpoint of the sages' and worthies' mind to rescue the times: regarding the congestion in the channels of personnel selection and evaluation, and regarding the supernumerary officers in the guards and battalions, if we strive to clarify the laws of demotion and promotion, then it will be appropriate; otherwise, the worthy and the unworthy will be confounded, and it will not do. Regarding the high price of grain during dearth, and regarding the migration of the people due to poverty, if we strive to prohibit the selfish exactions of rapacious officials, then it will be appropriate; otherwise, both Heaven and men will be filled with indignation, and it will not do. To set forth these four tasks so that they are necessariamente suited to the times is simply like this—why should Your Majesty need to seek elsewhere? In antiquity, Yu thought that if anyone in the world were drowning, it was as if he himself had drowned them; Ji thought that if anyone in the world were starving, it was as if he himself had starved them. If one can model oneself on the minds of Yu and Ji and be urgent in rescuing the times, thereby establishing offices and assigning duties, issuing policies and dispensing benevolence, what difficulty would there be in placing this age into the harmonious prosperity of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? If, however, in appointing only the worthy to office one departs from the institutions of the Officers of Zhou (Zhouguan), or in warding off disasters and averting calamities one falls short of the "Milky Way" ("Yunhan") ode, then it is not that the various affairs are unsuited to the times, but rather that the way they are managed has missed the time. Your servant therefore raises this as a warning to those who are lax in rescuing the times.

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
時可行而不行不文之遠於事情則不可行矯四臣
之偏必合於道如此
陛下亦將焉用哉古之舜聞一善言若决江河禹聞一昌
言下車以拜能法舜禹之心急於行道于以都俞戒
飭臣隣賛襄躋斯世於唐虞三代之泰和奚有耶若
使中郎補闕者出綰淮南之綬博士對策者往持江
都之麾則非言議不合於道所以聽之失其道耳臣
故舉此以為沮於行道者之戒也臣生長於鳳儀獸
舞之世樂育於鳶飛魚躍之天願為帝臣懷忠欲吐
謹述平昔
===
聖恩之所造就師友之所講明者已略陳其忠悃一二於
前矣
陛下策之篇終其慮臣等虛騁浮詞不切於世道且責之曰
朕將親覽而資治焉臣捧誦再三誠惶誠恐稽首頓首再
拜而言曰大哉
皇言乎一哉
皇心乎其所以廣開言路旁通下情必欲見諸行事以嘉
惠臣民之意至矣盡矣臣亦以為
陛下所以策臣徒究世變之汙隆不親
睿覽以資治焉雖勤勤問之夫何益臣等所以入對

時可行，而不行、不文之遠於事情，則不可行。矯四臣之偏，必合於道。如此，陛下亦將焉用哉？古之舜聞一善言，若决江河；禹聞一昌言，下車以拜。能法舜、禹之心，急於行道，于以都俞戒飭、臣隣賛襄，躋斯世於唐、虞、三代之泰和，奚有耶？若使中郎補闕者出綰淮南之綬，博士對策者往持江都之麾，則非言議不合於道，所以聽之失其道耳。臣故舉此以為沮於行道者之戒也。
臣生長於鳳儀獸舞之世，樂育於鳶飛魚躍之天，願為帝臣，懷忠欲吐，謹述平昔聖恩之所造就、師友之所講明者，已略陳其忠悃一二於前矣。陛下策之篇終，其慮臣等虛騁浮詞，不切於世道，且責之曰：「朕將親覽而資治焉。」臣捧誦再三，誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首，再拜而言曰：大哉皇言乎！一哉皇心乎！其所以廣開言路，旁通下情，必欲見諸行事，以嘉惠臣民之意，至矣盡矣。臣亦以為陛下所以策臣，徒究世變之汙隆，不親睿覽以資治焉，雖勤勤問之，夫何益？臣等所以入對，

Correcting the biases of these four ministers must bring them into conformity with the Way. Even so, how will Your Majesty make use of them? In antiquity, when Shun heard a single good word, he responded like a bursting river or stream; when Yu heard a single splendid word, he alighted from his carriage to bow. If one can model oneself on the minds of Shun and Yu, urgently putting the Way into practice—thereby exchanging courtly affirmations and admonitions while neighboring ministers assist and support—what difficulty would there be in raising this age to the supreme harmony of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? Yet if the Gentleman of the Interior who rectifies omissions [i.e.,汲黯 Ji An] is sent out to wear the seal-ribbon of Huainan, or the Erudite who answers the policy question [i.e., 董仲舒 Dong Zhongshu] goes off to hold the standard of Jiangdu, then it is not that their counsel failed to conform to the Way, but rather that in listening to them, the Way was lost. Your servant therefore cites these examples as a warning against those who are deterred from putting the Way into practice.

Your servant, born and raised in an age where phoenixes posture and beasts dance, and joyfully nurtured under a sky where hawks soar and fishes leap, desires to be an imperial minister, harboring loyalty that he longs to pour forth. Having respectfully recounted what in ordinary times was cultivated by Sacred Grace and elucidated by teachers and friends, I have already briefly set forth one or two points of my loyal sincerity above. At the close of Your Majesty's policy question, concerned lest your servants vainly indulge in floating rhetoric irrelevant to the Way of the world, You further charged us, saying: "We shall personally review them to aid in governance." Holding your words and reciting them again and again, your servant is truly awestruck and fearful; bowing his head to the ground and kowtowing twice, he speaks: Great indeed are the Imperial words! Unified indeed is the Imperial mind! title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
泛論世道之興衰不獲
天聽以佐治焉雖詨詨誦之夫何功今
陛下之所問者切於時以訪於道矣愚臣之所荅者因其
時以明其道矣伏願
陛下心領神會探其要領以端出治之本不專事於口耳
文字之間實體驗於身心踐履之際譬之形影然欲
影之正必先立其形之端未有形不端而影正者也
譬之源流然欲流之清必先濬其源之潔未有源不
潔而流清者也故論天下之治道必本於
陛下之身心論
===
陛下之身心必本於始終之一敬盖心者一身之主宰萬
事之本根心之存不存顧敬與不敬何如耳敬者德
之輿千聖傳心之法即所謂欽也唐虞君臣相傳相
戒固惟在於此也仲虺告湯亦曰欽崇天道尚父告
武王亦曰敬勝怠者吉是創業垂統者在此敬也周
公告王亦曰文王緝熈敬止召公告王亦曰曷其奈
何弗敬是持盈守成者在此敬也
陛下撫盈成之運紹熈洽之治
宗社生靈之所附屬人才國計之所關係天地鬼神之所
鑒察華夷上下之所觀瞻以一人之身繫天下之重

punctuated: 泛論世道之興衰，不獲天聽以佐治焉，雖詨詨誦之，夫何功？今陛下之所問者，切於時以訪於道矣；愚臣之所荅者，因其時以明其道矣。伏願陛下心領神會，探其要領，以端出治之本，不專事於口耳文字之間，實體驗於身心踐履之際。譬之形影然，欲影之正，必先立其形之端，未有形不端而影正者也；譬之源流然，欲流之清，必先濬其源之潔，未有源不潔而流清者也。故論天下之治道，必本於陛下之身心；論陛下之身心，必本於始終之一敬。盖心者，一身之主宰，萬事之本根，心之存不存，顧敬與不敬何如耳。敬者，德之輿，千聖傳心之法，即所謂「欽」也。唐虞君臣相傳相戒，固惟在於此也。仲虺告湯，亦曰「欽崇天道」；尚父告武王，亦曰「敬勝怠者吉」，是創業垂統者在此敬也。周公告王，亦曰「文王緝熈敬止」；召公告王，亦曰「曷其奈何弗敬」，是持盈守成者在此敬也。陛下撫盈成之運，紹熈洽之治，宗社生靈之所附屬，人才國計之所關係，天地鬼神之所鑒察，華夷上下之所觀瞻，以一人之身，繫天下之重，
translation_en: …merely discuss in broad generalities the rise and decline of the Way in the world without gaining Your Heavenly Hearing so as to assist in governance, even though we recite our words clamorously, what merit would there be in it? Now what Your Majesty has asked is relevant to the times in inquiring after the Way; and what Your foolish servant has answered proceeds from the times in order to clarify the Way. I humbly pray that Your Majesty will grasp it in mind and spirit and probe its essential points so as to rectify the root from which governance issues—not devoting effort solely to spoken words and written texts, but truly experiencing and embodying it in the practice of Your own person and mind. Take for example form and shadow: if one wishes the shadow to be straight, one must first set upright the posture of the form; there has never been a case where the form is not upright and yet the shadow is straight. Take for example source and stream: if one wishes the stream to be clear, one must first dredge the purity of its source; there has never been a case where the source is not pure and yet the stream is clear. Therefore, discussing the Way of governing the realm must be rooted in Your Majesty's person and mind; and discussing Your Majesty's person and mind must be rooted in a single reverence maintained from beginning to end. For the mind is the master of the entire person and the root of the myriad affairs; whether the mind is preserved or not depends simply on whether one is reverent or not. Reverence is the carriage of virtue; the method by which a thousand sages transmitted the mind is none other than what is called "reverential awe" (qin). That the rulers and ministers of Tang and Yu transmitted to and admonished one another assuredly lay solely in this. When Zhonghui advised Tang, he also said, "Reverently honor the Way of Heaven"; when Shangfu advised King Wu, he also said, "He whose reverence prevails over indolence will have good fortune"—thus those who founded dynasties and bequeathed a heritage relied upon this reverence. When the Duke of Zhou advised the King, he also said, "King Wen maintained continuous and bright reverence"; when the Duke of Shao advised the King, he also said, "Why and how could the King not be reverent?"—thus those who preserved fullness and maintained an established order relied upon this reverence. Your Majesty presides over an era of fullness and accomplishment and continues a reign of bright harmony, upon which the ancestral altars and the living people depend, with which men of talent and the plans of state are bound up, which Heaven, Earth, and the spirits scrutinize, and toward which Chinese and non-Chinese, superiors and inferiors all look up; with the person of One Man, You bear the weight of the entire realm,…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
一時不敬則一時於帝王之道有虧一事不敬則一
事於帝王之道有愧其思所以敬之哉其思所以敬
之哉敬之之道將若之何昕臨
大廷之敬必不忽於暗室屋漏之中日御
經筵之敬必不替於便僻侍從之所一念慮無非敬而
全體以立一動作無非敬而大用以行則君子大居
敬而體元居正之事備矣殆見燮理之功至而玉燭
均調聖統之典成而陰靄呈霽弓矢積武庫之塵老
稚鋤桑麻之影九夷八蠻賓服於
皇風清穆之餘五嶽四瀆效靈於
===
治教休明之日諸福之物難致之祥昔所未聞於今則
見即宋儒程子所謂上下一於恭敬則天地自位萬
物自育氣無不和而四靈畢至矣於此可以四三王
六五帝而唐虞三代太平之治亘萬古而僅兩見於
今日天下幸甚萬世幸甚臣一介草茅才不足以出膺
世用學不足以對揚
王休唯忠愛一念與生俱生故敢於
聖問之外竭其狂瞽始終以敬之功化證效為
陛下勸
陛下試采覽焉亦庶幾

經筵之敬必不替於便僻侍從之所一念慮無非敬而
全體以立一動作無非敬而大用以行則君子大居
敬而體元居正之事備矣始見爕理之功至而王燭
均調聖統之典成而陰騭呈needs矣積貳庫之塵老
稚鋤桑麻之影九夷八蠻賓服於
皇風清穆之餘五嶽四瀆效靈於
治教休明之日諸福之物難致之祥昔所未聞於今則
見即宋儒程子所謂上下一於恭敬則天地自位萬
物自育氣無不和而四靈畢至矣於此可以四三王
六五帝而唐虞三代太平之治亘萬古而僅兩見於
今日天下幸甚萬世幸甚臣一介草茅才不足以出膺
世用學不足以對揚
王休唯忠愛一念與生俱生故敢於
聖問之外竭其狂瞽始終以敬之功化證效爲
陛下勸
陛下試采覽焉亦庶幾
punctuated:
一時不敬，則一時於帝王之道有虧；一事不敬，則一事於帝王之道有愧。其思所以敬之哉！其思所以敬之哉！敬之之道將若之何？昕臨大廷之敬，必不忽於暗室屋漏之中；日御經筵之敬，必不替於便僻侍從之所。一念慮無非敬，而全體以立；一動作無非敬，而大用以行。則君子大居敬，而體元居正之事備矣。殆見燮理之功至，而玉燭均調；聖統之典成，而陰靄呈霽。弓矢積武庫之塵，老稚鋤桑麻之影。九夷八蠻，賓服於皇風清穆之餘；五嶽四瀆，效靈於治教休明之日。諸福之物，難致之祥，昔所未聞，於今則見。即宋儒程子所謂「上下一於恭敬，則天地自位，萬物自育，氣無不和，而四靈畢至」矣。於此可以四三王、六五帝，而唐虞三代太平之治，亘萬古而僅兩見於今日。天下幸甚！萬世幸甚！

臣一介草茅，才不足以出膺世用，學不足以對揚王休，唯忠愛一念，與生俱生，故敢於聖問之外，竭其狂瞽，始終以敬之功化證效為陛下勸。陛下試采覽焉，亦庶幾
translation_en:
… If for a single moment one is not reverent, then for that moment there is a deficiency in the Way of the Emperors and Kings; if in a single matter one is not reverent, then in that matter there is shame before the Way of the Emperors and Kings. May Your Majesty reflect on how to maintain reverence! May Your Majesty reflect on how to maintain reverence! What, then, is the way to maintain reverence? The reverence shown when attending the great court at dawn must never be neglected in the privacy of a dark room or the secluded corner of the house; the reverence shown when daily attending the Classics Colloquium must never be relaxed in the company of familiar favorites and attendants. When not a single thought is without reverence, the complete substance of the mind is established; when not a single action is without reverence, its great function is carried out. Thus the noble man's great abiding in reverence and the work of embodying the primal and dwelling in rectitude are made complete. Soon one will see the achievement of harmonizing governance reach its peak, and the jade candle of the four seasons shine in even harmony; the canons of the sagely succession will be fulfilled, and dark mists will clear into bright skies. Bows and arrows will gather dust in the armories, while the old and young hoe in the shade of mulberry and hemp. The Nine Yi and Eight Man tribes will submit as guests under the pure and solemn influence of the Imperial wind; the Five Marchmounts and Four Conduits will manifest their numinous efficacy in this day of illustrious governance and instruction. All manner of auspicious things and hard-to-obtain portents, unheard of in the past, will now appear. This is just what the Song-dynasty Confucian Master Cheng meant when he said: "When superior and inferior are united in respectful reverence, Heaven and Earth naturally take their proper places, the myriad things are naturally nurtured, the vital energies are completely harmonious, and the four numinous creatures all arrive." By this, Your Majesty can become the fourth alongside the Three Kings and the sixth alongside the Five Emperors, and the grand peace of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, across all antiquity, will be seen for only the second time today. How fortunate for the realm! How fortunate for ten thousand generations!

Your servant is a mere rustic from the thatched huts; my talent is insufficient to go forth and meet the needs of the age, and my learning is insufficient to respond to and extol the royal beneficence. Only a single thought of loyalty and affection has been with me since birth. Therefore I have dared, beyond the scope of Your Majesty's sagely inquiry, to exhaust my foolish and blind views, from beginning to end offering the transformative achievements and verified effects of reverence as an exhortation to Your Majesty. title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
臣董越
臣對臣聞惟辟奉天惟皇作極而操致治之柄在於
君包括治體啓沃君心而言致治之要在於臣盖天
下以一人為主而引君以當道為先君能操致治之
柄而不下移則以用人才而文武足以周一世之用
以賛化育而和氣足以遂萬姓之安此人君之尊所
以與天同體而有財成輔相之功也人臣能盡引君
之道而不敢惑以他岐則上而格君而君心無不格
下而言治而治效無不成此人臣之職所以與君有
相資而稱股肱耳目之任也君盡君道以致治而不
===
違臣盡臣道以言治而必切則何事之不可濟而何
弊之不可救何時之不可宜而何道之不可合哉唐
虞三代君臣之所以都俞吁咈於一堂而共成雍熙
泰和之治者用此道也欽惟
皇帝陛下以聖神文武之資備剛健中正之德紹承
大統五載于茲宵旰惓惓圖惟至理治已臻于
皇極而猶懷望道未見之心世已底於平康而方切視
民如傷之念廼於
萬幾之暇進臣等於
廷降賜

臣董越。

臣對：臣聞惟辟奉天，惟皇作極，而操致治之柄在於君；包括治體，啓沃君心，而言致治之要在於臣。盖天下以一人為主，而引君以當道為先。君能操致治之柄而不下移，則以用人才，而文武足以周一世之用；以賛化育，而和氣足以遂萬姓之安。此人君之尊所以與天同體，而有財成輔相之功也。人臣能盡引君之道，而不敢惑以他岐，則上而格君，而君心無不格；下而言治，而治效無不成。此人臣之職所以與君有相資，而稱股肱耳目之任也。君盡君道以致治而不違，臣盡臣道以言治而必切，則何事之不可濟，而何弊之不可救？何時之不可宜，而何道之不可合哉？唐虞三代君臣之所以都俞吁咈於一堂，而共成雍熙泰和之治者，用此道也。欽惟皇帝陛下，以聖神文武之資，備剛健中正之德，紹承大統，五載于茲，宵旰惓惓，圖惟至理。治已臻于皇極，而猶懷望道未見之心；世已底於平康，而方切視民如傷之念。廼於萬幾之暇，進臣等於廷，降賜
translation_en:
Your servant Dong Yue 董越.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that only the sovereign obeys Heaven and only the august ruler establishes the ultimate standard, so holding the handle for bringing about good governance lies with the ruler; encompassing the substance of governance and enlightening and enriching the ruler's mind, so speaking of the essentials for bringing about good governance, lies with the ministers. Indeed, all under Heaven takes the One Man as its master, and in guiding the ruler, placing him upon the proper Way comes first. If the ruler can hold the handle of bringing about good governance without letting it shift downward, then when he employs men of talent, civil and military officials will suffice to meet the needs of a whole generation; and when he assists in Heaven's transforming and nurturing work, harmonious vital energy will suffice to fulfill the peace and security of the myriad people. This is why the exalted position of the ruler shares one body with Heaven and achieves the merit of regulating, completing, assisting, and supporting. If a minister can fulfill the Way of guiding his ruler and dare not mislead him with other divergent paths, then above, in rectifying the ruler, the ruler's mind will never fail to be rectified; and below, in speaking of governance, the results of governance will never fail to be accomplished. This is why the duty of the minister is mutually supportive with the ruler and answers to the responsibility of being his limbs, ears, and eyes. When the ruler fulfills the Way of the ruler to bring about governance without deviation, and the minister fulfills the Way of the minister to speak of governance with unfailing relevance, then what affair cannot be accomplished, and what abuse cannot be remedied? What occasion cannot be suited, and what principle cannot be harmonized? That the rulers and ministers of the eras of Tang 唐, Yu 虞, and the Three Dynasties expressed agreement and dissent in a single hall and together achieved an era of harmonious and supreme peace was through the use of this Way.

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, endowed with sagely, divine, civil, and martial qualities, and possessing the virtues of vigorous strength and central rectitude, has succeeded to the Great Succession for five years now, dressing before dawn and eating after dusk in earnest devotion to planning for ultimate order. Governance has already reached the august ultimate standard, yet You still cherish the mind of gazing toward the Way as though not yet having seen it; the world has already arrived at peace and tranquility, yet You are just now earnestly filled with the thought of regarding the people as though they were wounded. Thereupon, in the leisure from Your myriad affairs of state, You have brought Your servants forward into the court and graciously bestowed…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
清問諮臣以當世之務責臣以盡言之誠臣有以知
陛下是心即古昔帝王兢兢業業不自滿假
祖宗
列聖用賢圖治孜孜汲汲之盛心矣顧臣愚陋曷足以奉
大對然而罄竭一得之迂愚以少裨
治道之萬一亦臣區區之素志也臣竊惟天下之事操
得其要則執簡可以御煩酌之有方則由今可以冠
古自古人君亮天之道莫要於用賢理民我
國家自
太祖高皇帝定鼎之初已著為令内而
===
京畿則設胄監以儲天下之英材外而郡縣則設學校
以育民間之俊秀三年大比既拔其賢者能者以任
用之以時充貢復儲其俊者秀者以預備之
列聖相承率由是道是即唐虞三代之家塾黨庠術序國
學三物賓興克知克用之遺意矣銓選之途何嘗壅
乎比年以來或繇邊儲未充而開納馬納粟之例或
繇大臣建議而立限年拔擢之法是雖
國家因時制宜之常古昔立賢無方之意而非臣愚之
所及知者然以今有限之位而待此無窮之才其酌
之之宜處之之要亦所當講也伏望

清問，諮臣以當世之務，責臣以盡言之誠。臣有以知陛下是心，即古昔帝王兢兢業業不自滿假，祖宗列聖用賢圖治、孜孜汲汲之盛心矣。顧臣愚陋，曷足以奉大對？然而罄竭一得之迂愚，以少裨治道之萬一，亦臣區區之素志也。

臣竊惟天下之事，操得其要，則執簡可以御煩；酌之有方，則由今可以冠古。自古人君亮天之道，莫要於用賢理民。我國家自太祖高皇帝定鼎之初，已著為令。内而京畿，則設胄監以儲天下之英材；外而郡縣，則設學校以育民間之俊秀。三年大比，既拔其賢者能者以任用之；以時充貢，復儲其俊者秀者以預備之。列聖相承，率由是道，是即唐虞三代之家塾、黨庠、術序、國學，三物賓興，克知克用之遺意矣，銓選之途何嘗壅乎？比年以來，或繇邊儲未充，而開納馬、納粟之例；或繇大臣建議，而立限年拔擢之法。是雖國家因時制宜之常，古昔立賢無方之意，而非臣愚之所及知者；然以今有限之位，而待此無窮之才，其酌之之宜、處之之要，亦所當講也。伏望
translation_en:
…Your sagely inquiry, consulting Your servant on the affairs of the present age and charging Your servant with the sincerity of speaking without reserve. Your servant thus knows that this mind of Your Majesty is none other than the grand mind of the emperors and kings of antiquity, who were cautious and attentive and never self-satisfied, and of Your Imperial Ancestors and the successive sage emperors, who tirelessly and assiduously employed the worthy to plan for good governance. Yet given Your servant's foolishness and vulgarity, how could he be adequate to offer a great reply? Nevertheless, to exhaust the pedantic foolishness of a single humble insight in order to contribute even one ten-thousandth to the way of governance is also Your servant's modest, long-held aspiration.

Your servant venture to reflect that in the affairs of the realm, if one grasps their essentials, one can hold to simplicity to govern complexity; if one deliberates upon them with the proper method, one can proceed from the present to surpass antiquity. Since antiquity, in a ruler's way of assisting Heaven, nothing has been more essential than employing the worthy and governing the people. In our dynasty, from the very beginning when Emperor Gaozu (Taizu) established the dynastic rule, this was already enacted as an ordinance. Within, in the capital prefectures, the Directorate of Education (Zhoujian) was established to store up the outstanding talents of the realm; without, in the prefectures and counties, schools were established to nurture the eminent and refined among the people. At the triennial grand competition, the worthy and the capable are selected to be appointed and employed; through the periodic presentation of tribute students, the eminent and the refined are further stored up in reserve. The successive sage emperors have inherited this from one another, all following this path. This is indeed the enduring intent of the family schools (jiashu), district academies (dangxiang), regional colleges (shuxu), and state university (guoxue) of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, of the ceremonial recommendation of the talented on the basis of the Three Things, and of truly knowing and truly employing them—how then was the path of official selection and appointment ever congested? In recent years, however, either because frontier provisions were not yet sufficient, the regulations for contributing horses and contributing grain to enter the service were opened; or because grand ministers submitted proposals, the method of promotion by fixed age limits was established. Although this is the normal practice of the state in adapting measures to the times and reflects the ancient intent of establishing the worthy without fixed bounds—matters beyond what Your foolish servant is capable of comprehending—still, when using the finite positions of the present to await this inexhaustible supply of talent, the appropriateness of deliberating upon them and the essentials of managing them are also things that ought to be discussed. 陛下操黜陟之柄於上嚴考察之令於下申命大臣按行
方嶽不職者雖非久任而必去貪墨者雖有才美而
不留而又限以學校之員一如
祖宗舊制杜其雜進之路以塞徼倖之門凡在選部之末
仕而願乞閑者虛其爵號以榮之既仕而樂引去者
異其恩數以旌之則自然名利相均而不至於壅滯
矣自古人君經國之道莫要於選將馭兵我
國家自
太祖高皇帝垂統以来已有定制内設五府以總其綱外
設衞所以理其紀握將機者非勲閥而不授掌戎伍
===
者非軍功則不遷百年于茲循用是道是即唐虞三
代之詰爾戎兵張皇六師德懋懋官功懋懋賞之遺
意矣衞所之員何嘗濫乎近年来承襲者不聞有
所簡選而肉食者每充斥於要津論功者未聞有所
顧惜而冒進者多混淆乎名器是雖
國家功疑惟重賞延於世之大恩而非臣愚所敢輕議
者然以十人營屯之資而不足一人坐食之費其裁
省之要斟酌之方亦所當講也伏望
陛下操予奪之柄於上著澄汰之令於下廷選大臣按行
藩閫老不勝任者限之以更替勇敢有為者進之以

陛下操黜陟之柄於上，嚴考察之令於下，申命大臣，按行方嶽。不職者雖非久任而必去，貪墨者雖有才美而不留。而又限以學校之員，一如祖宗舊制，杜其雜進之路，以塞徼倖之門。凡在選部之末仕而願乞閑者，虛其爵號以榮之；既仕而樂引去者，異其恩數以旌之。則自然名利相均，而不至於壅滯矣。
自古人君經國之道，莫要於選將馭兵。我國家自太祖高皇帝垂統以来，已有定制：内設五府以總其綱，外設衞所以理其紀；握將機者非勲閥而不授，掌戎伍者非軍功則不遷。百年于茲，循用是道，是即唐虞三代之詰爾戎兵、張皇六師，德懋懋官、功懋懋賞之遺意矣，衞所之員何嘗濫乎？近年来，承襲者不聞有所簡選，而肉食者每充斥於要津；論功者未聞有所顧惜，而冒進者多混淆乎名器。是雖國家功疑惟重、賞延於世之大恩，而非臣愚所敢輕議者；然以十人營屯之資，而不足一人坐食之費，其裁省之要、斟酌之方，亦所當講也。伏望陛下操予奪之柄於上，著澄汰之令於下，廷選大臣，按行藩閫。老不勝任者，限之以更替；勇敢有為者，進之以
translation_en:
…Your Majesty will wield the authority of demotion and promotion from above, enforce strict orders of personnel evaluation below, and instruct high officials to tour and inspect the provincial jurisdictions. Those who are derelict in duty, even if they have not held office long, must be dismissed; those who are venal and corrupt, even if they possess fine talents, must not be retained. Furthermore, restrict the quota of students in the state schools strictly in accordance with the old statutes of the Imperial Ancestors, blocking avenues of irregular advancement so as to close the door to opportunistic fortune-seeking. As for all those awaiting appointment in the Ministry of Personnel who have not yet taken office [reading 末仕 as 未仕] and wish to ask for retirement, honor them with nominal titles of rank; and as for those already in office who are happy to withdraw, distinguish them with special marks of grace. Then fame and practical interest will naturally be balanced, and the path of selection will not become congested.

Since antiquity, in a ruler's way of governing the state, nothing has been more vital than selecting generals and commanding troops. Since Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), established our dynasty's succession, there have been fixed institutions: in the capital, the Five Chief Military Commissions were established to control the main principles; in the provinces, Guards and Battalions were established to regulate the details. Those holding generalships were not appointed unless they came from families of meritorious nobility, and those commanding the ranks were not promoted unless they had achieved military merit. For a hundred years now, this way has been followed. This is indeed the inherited intent of the era of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties in "putting your weaponry in order," "displaying in grandeur the Six Armies," and "to great virtue giving great office, to great merit giving great reward." How could the officers of the Guards and Battalions ever have become excessive?

In recent years, however, one does not hear of any selection being exercised over those who inherit their posts, so that mere "meat-eaters" constantly crowd into key positions; and one does not hear of any scrupulousness among those who evaluate military merit, so that fraudulent climbers often confound official titles and ranks. Although this stems from the dynasty's great grace—whereby in cases of doubtful merit, the reward is made heavy, and rewards are extended to subsequent generations—and is not something your foolish servant dares lightly criticize, nevertheless, when the resources produced by ten men farming in military colonies are insufficient to cover the cost of one man sitting idle and eating, the essentials of retrenchment and the methods of careful adjustment must also be discussed. I humbly hope Your Majesty will wield the authority of granting and depriving from above, promulgate orders for weeding out the superfluous below, and select high officials at court to tour and inspect the frontier and regional military commands. For those too old and unequal to their duties, set rules for their replacement; for those who are brave and capable of action, advance them through…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
超遷而又參酌重輕權衡虛實凡賞賚之可以代陞
者不以其實費而不與旌別之可以勸功者不以其
飾虛而不加則自然虛實相濟而不至有溢員矣歲
無常稔者天之道土有常懷者人之情故陰陽有愆
伏灾沴之流行雖以帝堯之仁而不免於九年之水
雖以成湯之聖而不免於七年之旱以盤庚之遷殷
而安土重遷且不能已於大家世族而况於近年以
来或加以水旱之相仍或病於守令之屠剥則貴糴
以免餒轉徙以求生何能免哉伏蒙
陛下垂天地之至仁不忍赤子之困阨諮臣以綏輯之術
===
拯救之方臣愚不能自裁敢竊誦
聖策所謂常平有法誠可倣而為之也均田有制誠可稽
而行之也夫常平之法肇於李悝至漢耿壽昌因之
其法以穀賤則增價而糴以利農穀貴則減價而糶
以利民雖盡非周官荒政十二之法要亦可以免夫
歉則糶貴貧則民徙之憂矣均田之制出於李安世
而後魏因之其制則男子四十畝婦人二十畝戶絕
者為公田丁多者則增給以至縣令刺史皆有等差
雖非古人分田制禄之常要亦可以免夫富連阡陌
貧無卓錐之歎矣

punctuated:
超遷。而又參酌重輕，權衡虛實，凡賞賚之可以代陞者，不以其實費而不與；旌別之可以勸功者，不以其飾虛而不加，則自然虛實相濟，而不至有溢員矣。

歲無常稔者，天之道；土有常懷者，人之情。故陰陽有愆伏、灾沴之流行，雖以帝堯之仁，而不免於九年之水；雖以成湯之聖，而不免於七年之旱。以盤庚之遷殷，而安土重遷，且不能已於大家世族，而况於近年以来，或加以水旱之相仍，或病於守令之屠剥，則貴糴以免餒、轉徙以求生，何能免哉？伏蒙陛下垂天地之至仁，不忍赤子之困阨，諮臣以綏輯之術、拯救之方。臣愚不能自裁，敢竊誦聖策所謂「常平有法」，誠可倣而為之也；「均田有制」，誠可稽而行之也。夫常平之法肇於李悝，至漢耿壽昌因之，其法以穀賤則增價而糴以利農，穀貴則減價而糶以利民。雖盡非《周官》荒政十二之法，要亦可以免夫歉則糶貴、貧則民徙之憂矣。均田之制出於李安世，而後魏因之，其制則男子四十畝，婦人二十畝，戶絕者為公田，丁多者則增給，以至縣令、刺史皆有等差。雖非古人分田制禄之常，要亦可以免夫富連阡陌、貧無卓錐之歎矣。
translation_en:
…rapid promotion. Furthermore, if You weigh relative importance and balance nominal honors against material rewards—so that whenever material rewards can substitute for promotion in rank, they are not withheld on account of their actual expenditure, and whenever commendation and distinction can encourage merit, they are not omitted on account of being merely nominal adornment—then nominal and material incentives will naturally complement one another, and there will not come to be superfluous personnel.

That harvests are not always abundant is the Way of Heaven; that people always cherish their native soil is human nature. Thus, when yin and yang suffer imbalances and calamities spread, even with the benevolence of Emperor Yao, nine years of floods could not be avoided; even with the sageliness of Tang the Successful (Cheng Tang), seven years of drought could not be avoided. When Pan Geng moved the Yin capital, attachment to native soil and reluctance to relocate could not be prevented even among great houses and hereditary clans—how much more so in recent years, when people are either afflicted by successive floods and droughts or harmed by the ruthless extortion of Grand Coordinators, Prefects, and Magistrates! How then could they avoid buying grain at high prices to escape starvation, or wandering from place to place in search of survival? Humbly, Your Majesty has extended the supreme benevolence of Heaven and Earth, unable to bear the distress of Your infant subjects, and has consulted Your servant on the arts of pacification and settlement and the methods of rescue and relief. In my folly I cannot devise them on my own, yet I venture to repeat what Your Majesty's sacred policy question states: "there is a method for Ever-Normal Granaries," which indeed can be emulated and put into practice; and "there is a system for Equal-Field land allotment," which indeed can be examined and carried out. Now, the method of the Ever-Normal Granary (changping) originated with Li Kui, and in the Han dynasty Geng Shouchang built upon it. By this method, when grain is cheap, it is bought up at an increased price in order to benefit the farmers; when grain is dear, it is sold off at a reduced price in order to benefit the people. Although this is not entirely the same as the twelve famine-relief policies (huangzheng) in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), in essence it can still avert the worry of grain being sold at high prices in lean years and the people migrating in poverty. The system of Equal-Field land allotment (juntian) came from Li Anshi, and the Later Wei dynasty built upon it. Under this system, a man received forty mou and a woman twenty mou; the land of extinguished households became public land, and households with many adult males received additional allocations, while everyone up to District Magistrates and Regional Inspectors received allotments graded by rank. Although this is not the constant norm of the ancients in dividing land and fixing emoluments, in essence it can still avert the lament that the rich own lands stretching across the paths while the poor lack ground enough to stand an awl.

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
陛下誠能操是數者之柄於上而責是數者之任於臣將
見文武兼資德威並用大而論道經邦燮理陰陽者
有其人次而六卿分職典司政教者有其人外之則
藩閫之重足以為干城守令之賢足以宣德化疆埸
不患乎無韓范之儒禁中不患乎無頗牧之輩禮樂
以之而脩明紀綱以之而振舉蒼生以之而富庶夷
狄以之而賓服上而天地之道賴之以財成下而萬
姓之繁資之以生遂真可以四三王而六五帝陋漢
唐宋於不居矣尚何慮夫才不足以周一世之用而
治不足以致萬姓之安哉若乃致此之道必有至言
===
陛下固已斷自
淵衷試諸事為矣而猶舉以策臣者是即大舜好察邇
言之意昔人詢于芻蕘之義也臣聞之大學有曰古
之欲明明德於天下者先治其國欲治其國者先齊
其家欲齊其家者先脩其身欲脩其身者先正其心
欲正其心者先誠其意欲誠其意者先致其知致知
在格物中庸曰致中和天地位焉萬物育焉然自三
代以後獻言者能合此而不違體此而不失者百無
一二漢之董仲舒大廷三對黃鐘大呂似則似矣然
而屑屑於縱陰閉陽其視中庸致中致和之說為何

陛下固已斷自
淵衷試諸事為矣而猶舉以策〔臣若〕〔是即〕大舜好察邇
言之意昔人詢于芻蕘之義也〔臣聞〕之大學有曰古
之欲明明德於天下者先治其國欲治其國者先齊
