在格物中庸曰致中和天地位焉萬物育焉然自三
代以後覈言者能合此而不違體此而不失者百無
一二漢之董仲舒大廷三對黃鍾大呂似則似矣然
而屑屑於縱陰閉陽以其視中庸致中致和之說為何
punctuated: 陛下誠能操是數者之柄於上，而責是數者之任於臣，將見文武兼資，德威並用；大而論道經邦、燮理陰陽者有其人，次而六卿分職、典司政教者有其人；外之則藩閫之重足以為干城，守令之賢足以宣德化；疆埸不患乎無韓、范之儒，禁中不患乎無頗、牧之輩。禮樂以之而脩明，紀綱以之而振舉，蒼生以之而富庶，夷狄以之而賓服；上而天地之道賴之以財成，下而萬姓之繁資之以生遂，真可以四三王而六五帝，陋漢、唐、宋於不居矣。尚何慮夫才不足以周一世之用，而治不足以致萬姓之安哉？若乃致此之道，必有至言，陛下固已斷自淵衷，試諸事為矣，而猶舉以策臣者，是即大舜好察邇言之意，昔人詢于芻蕘之義也。臣聞之《大學》有曰：「古之欲明明德於天下者，先治其國；欲治其國者，先齊其家；欲齊其家者，先脩其身；欲脩其身者，先正其心；欲正其心者，先誠其意；欲誠其意者，先致其知，致知在格物。」《中庸》曰：「致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。」然自三代以後，獻言者能合此而不違、體此而不失者，百無一二。漢之董仲舒大廷三對，黃鐘大呂，似則似矣，然而屑屑於縱陰閉陽，其視《中庸》致中致和之說為何
translation_en:
If Your Majesty can truly wield the authority over these several matters from above and hold your ministers responsible for carrying them out, we shall soon see civil and military talents drawn upon together, and virtue and majesty employed in tandem. On the highest level, there will be the right men to discourse on the Way, govern the state, and harmonize yin and yang; next, there will be the right men among the Six Ministers to divide responsibilities and take charge of governance and education. In the provinces, the weighty commanders of the frontiers and regional defenses will suffice to serve as shields and bulwarks, while worthy Prefects and Magistrates will suffice to propagate your virtuous transformation. On the borders, there will be no worry over a lack of Confucian statesmen like Han Qi 韓琦 and Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹; within the forbidden palace, there will be no worry over a lack of generals like Lian Po 廉頗 and Li Mu 李牧. Through this, rites and music will be cultivated and made illustrious, laws and institutions will be invigorated and upheld, the common people will become prosperous and numerous, and the border tribes will submit in allegiance. Above, the Way of Heaven and Earth will rely on this for its regulation and completion; below, the multitude of the myriad people will depend on this for their livelihood and fulfillment. Truly, you will be able to stand as a fourth to the Three Kings and a sixth to the Five Emperors, disdaining to dwell on the level of Han, Tang, and Song. What further worry could there be that talent might not suffice to meet the needs of the whole age, or that governance might not suffice to bring peace to the myriad people?

As for the Way to achieve this, there must be words of ultimate truth. Your Majesty has assuredly already decided upon them in the depths of your heart and tested them in practical affairs. That you nevertheless raise them to question your servant in this policy examination exemplifies Great Shun's 舜 fondness for examining near-at-hand words, and the ancient principle of consulting even grass- and firewood-gatherers. Your servant has heard that the Great Learning (Daxue) says: "The ancients who wished to illustrate illustrious virtue throughout the empire first ordered well their own states. Wishing to order well their states, they first regulated their families. Wishing to regulate their families, they first cultivated their persons. Wishing to cultivate their persons, they first rectified their hearts. Wishing to rectify their hearts, they first sought to be sincere in their thoughts. Wishing to be sincere in their thoughts, they first extended to the utmost their knowledge. Such extension of knowledge lay in the investigation of things." And the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) says: "Let the states of equilibrium and harmony exist in perfection, and a happy order will prevail throughout heaven and earth, and all things will be nourished and flourish." Yet since the Three Dynasties, among those who have offered counsel, scarcely one or two in a hundred have been able to conform to this without straying and embody this without fail. In the Han dynasty, Dong Zhongshu's 董仲舒 three replies in the great court resonated like the Yellow Bell and Great Tube pitch-pipes—impressive as they seemed, he nonetheless busied himself with petty details of releasing yin and shutting off yang. Compared to the teaching of achieving equilibrium and harmony in the Doctrine of the Mean, how…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
若拘拘於災祥符應其視大學新民新命之意為何
如鼂錯之洋洋大對與董齊聲美則美矣然而刑名
其學果聖賢脩齊治平之學乎術數其歸果聖賢大
中至正之歸乎故宋儒蘇洵嘗謂董生得聖人之經
其失也流而為迂鼂錯得聖人之權其失也流而為
詐由是言之則其道術之未底於純獻言之未合於
道亦可見矣賈誼政事一書通達國體非不辯矣然
而詞傷激切致帝之謙讓未遑豈非不密之過乎張
良之為帝者師功成身退非不智矣然而學宗黃老
致帝之治雜伯功豈非不文之弊乎故宋儒蘇軾嘗
===
謂陸贄之智如子房而文則過辯如賈誼而術不疎
即此觀之則其學術之有偏引君之無術又可知矣
雖然
陛下之策臣者臣既畧陳其由矣而於終篇猶欲責臣以
陳四者之務必宜於時矯四臣之偏必合於道且
寵之以將覽以資治之詞臣愚誠不知所自出然嘗聞
之人主開求言之路必將有聽言之實人臣遇得言
之秋不可無獻言之誠盖求言之路不常開而得言
之秋不易遇今
陛下開求言之路而臣遇得言之秋

若？拘拘於災祥符應，其視《大學》新民新命之意為何如？鼂錯之洋洋大對，與董齊聲，美則美矣；然而刑名其學，果聖賢脩齊治平之學乎？術數其歸，果聖賢大中至正之歸乎？故宋儒蘇洵嘗謂：「董生得聖人之經，其失也流而為迂；鼂錯得聖人之權，其失也流而為詐。」由是言之，則其道術之未底於純，獻言之未合於道，亦可見矣。賈誼《政事》一書，通達國體，非不辯矣；然而詞傷激切，致帝之謙讓未遑，豈非不密之過乎？張良之為帝者師，功成身退，非不智矣；然而學宗黃老，致帝之治雜伯功，豈非不文之弊乎？故宋儒蘇軾嘗謂：「陸贄之智如子房而文則過，辯如賈誼而術不疎。」即此觀之，則其學術之有偏，引君之無術，又可知矣。
雖然，陛下之策臣者，臣既畧陳其由矣；而於終篇猶欲責臣以陳四者之務必宜於時，矯四臣之偏必合於道，且寵之以「將覽以資治」之詞。臣愚，誠不知所自出。然嘗聞之：人主開求言之路，必將有聽言之實；人臣遇得言之秋，不可無獻言之誠。盖求言之路不常開，而得言之秋不易遇。今陛下開求言之路，而臣遇得言之秋；
translation_en:
… compare to the doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) on achieving equilibrium and harmony? And in his pedantic preoccupation with portents of disaster and auspicious omens, how does he compare to the meaning of renewing the people and renewing the Mandate in the Great Learning (Daxue)? As for Chao Cuo 鼂錯, his expansive grand responses shared equal fame with Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒—admirable indeed! Yet his learning was that of Legalist names and punishments: was it truly the sages' and worthies' learning of self-cultivation, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world? His ultimate recourse was to tactical statecraft: was it truly the sages' and worthies' ultimate recourse to great centrality and utmost correctness? Thus the Song-dynasty Confucian scholar Su Xun 蘇洵 once said: "Master Dong grasped the constant standard of the sages, yet his flaw was to degenerate into pedantry; Chao Cuo grasped the权变 (expediency) of the sages, yet his flaw was to degenerate into deceit." Spoken of in this light, it can also be seen that their techniques of the Way had not yet reached purity, and the counsel they offered did not yet accord with the Way. As for Jia Yi's 賈誼 memorial On Governance (Zhengshi), it thoroughly comprehended the fundamental principles of the state and was by no means lacking in eloquence; yet his words suffered from being overly vehement and urgent, causing the Emperor to modestly decline for lack of leisure—was this not the fault of lacking circumspection? As for Zhang Liang 張良 acting as teacher to an emperor and retiring once his merit was achieved, he was by no means lacking in wisdom; yet his learning took Huang-Lao 黃老 as its ancestor, causing the Emperor's governance to be mixed with the achievements of a hegemon—was this not the defect of lacking cultural refinement? Thus the Song-dynasty Confucian scholar Su Shi 蘇軾 once said: "Lu Zhi's 陸贄 wisdom was like that of Zifang 子房 [Zhang Liang], yet he surpassed him in literary refinement; his eloquence was like that of Jia Yi, yet his statecraft was not careless." Viewed from this perspective, it can further be known that their scholarship had its biases and that they lacked the proper art of guiding their sovereign.

Even so, regarding the questions Your Majesty has posed to Your servant in this policy question, Your servant has already briefly set forth their principles. Yet at the close of the text, You still wish to charge Your servant with setting forth how the tasks of those four matters must be suited to the times, and how rectifying the biases of those four ministers must accord with the Way; and You have further graced me with the words that You "will peruse them to aid in governance." Your servant is foolish and truly does not know where to begin. Yet I have heard it said: when a sovereign opens the path for seeking counsel, he must possess the substance of heeding counsel; when a subject encounters a season in which he is permitted to speak, he cannot be without the sincerity of offering counsel. For the path of seeking counsel is not always open, and the season for being permitted to speak is not easily encountered. Now Your Majesty has opened the path for seeking counsel, and Your servant has encountered a season for being permitted to speak; …

事無不繫於人君之一身尤無不繫於人君之一心
陛下以不世出之資當大有為之日自
嗣登大寳以来凡擇材以理民核功以馭兵與凡敬天
之道勤民之要法古之宜聽言之實一惟總之以一

祖宗

===

punctuated: 陛下有聽言之實，而臣可無獻言之誠乎？臣竊惟天下之事，無不繫於人君之一身，尤無不繫於人君之一心。陛下以不世出之資，當大有為之日，自嗣登大寳以来，凡擇材以理民，核功以馭兵，與凡敬天之道、勤民之要、法古之宜、聽言之實，一惟總之以一身，断之以一心，惟古昔之聖帝明王與祖宗列聖之舊章成憲是守是若，真足以措斯世於平康，納斯民於皇極，以隆我國家億萬載太平之福矣。而臣愚猶欲以「操大柄」之一言、「本諸心」之一語為陛下獻者，盖陛下之德雖不可以有加，而臣子愛上之誠，毎惓惓然有加而無已，亦向陽之葵藿、委澗之畎澮也。伏惟陛下留神於用人亮天之間，洞察於進言納忠之際，慎名器而不輕畀，使爵位皆足以待功德之人；召和氣以富蒼生，使凶荒不足以勞宵旰之慮；有言逆于心，必求之於道；有言遜于志，必求
translation_en: … Your Majesty possesses the true substance of heeding counsel—how then could your servant lack the sincerity to offer it? Your servant humbly reflects that among the affairs of the world, there is none that does not depend upon the person of the ruler alone, and even more so, none that does not depend upon the mind of the ruler alone. Endowed with talents that appear but once in an age, and meeting a time of great enterprise, since ascending the great throne by succession, in all matters of selecting talent to govern the people and verifying merit to command the troops, as well as the way of revering Heaven, the essentials of being diligent for the people, the suitability of modeling on antiquity, and the substance of heeding counsel, Your Majesty has wholly united them in your own person and decided them with your own mind. Only the established statutes and settled constitutions of the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity, together with those of the Imperial Ancestors and Successive Sages, do you uphold and conform to. Truly, this suffices to place this age in peace and tranquility, to bring these people into the August Ultimate, and to exalt the blessings of great peace for our dynasty for hundreds of millions of years. Yet your foolish servant still wishes to offer Your Majesty the phrase "wielding the great handle of authority" and the expression "rooting it in the mind." For although nothing can be added to Your Majesty's virtue, a subject's sincere love for his Sovereign is ever earnestly increasing without cease—just like sunflowers and bean leaves turning toward the sun, or field ditches pouring into a mountain stream. Your servant humbly prays that Your Majesty will fix your attention upon employing men and assisting Heaven's work, and exercise keen insight when counsel is presented and loyalty is received: guard official titles and emblems of rank and do not bestow them lightly, so that noble ranks and offices all suffice to await men of merit and virtue; summon harmonious vital energy to enrich the common people, so that famine and dearth do not suffice to trouble your anxious thoughts from before dawn until after dark; when words run counter to your mind, be sure to seek whether they accord with the Way; when words are agreeable to your will, be sure to seek…

title: 成化五年進士登科錄
text:
諸非道迂疎者於道或有合而不必遺辯智者於道
有未合而不必與將見賢能效職而感召和氣之有
人忠讜日聞而贊襄治化之有頼事雖有如四者之
當務不必慮無以處之言雖有如四臣之有偏不必
慮無以察之矣臣學術淺疎叨塵
賜對於前四者之務陳之未宜於時於後四臣之偏矯
之未合乎道愛
君一念之誠發於天性惟
陛下恕其狂妄少
垂仁而採納焉則臣愚幸甚天下幸甚臣干冒
===
天威不勝戰慄之至臣謹對

人忠讜日聞而贊襄治化之有賴事雖有如四者之

慮無以察之矣臣學術淺踈叨塵
賜對於前四者之務陳之未宜於時於後四臣之偏矯
之未合乎道愛
君一念之誠發於天性惟
陛下恕其狂妄少
垂仁而採納焉則臣愚幸甚天下幸甚臣干冒
天威不勝戰慄之至臣謹對
punctuated: 諸非道；迂疎者於道或有合而不必遺，辯智者於道有未合而不必與。將見賢能效職，而感召和氣之有人；忠讜日聞，而贊襄治化之有頼。事雖有如四者之當務，不必慮無以處之；言雖有如四臣之有偏，不必慮無以察之矣。臣學術淺疎，叨塵賜對。於前四者之務，陳之未宜於時；於後四臣之偏，矯之未合乎道。愛君一念之誠，發於天性。惟陛下恕其狂妄，少垂仁而採納焉，則臣愚幸甚，天下幸甚。臣干冒天威，不勝戰慄之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: … whether they are contrary to the Way; those who are pedantic and impractical may yet accord with the Way in some respect and need not be discarded, while those who are eloquent and clever may fail to accord with the Way and need not be approved. Then we shall see the worthy and capable fulfilling their duties, so that there will be men to evoke and summon harmonious ether; loyal and forthright words will be heard daily, so that there will be support in assisting and furthering transformative governance. Even when affairs involve urgent tasks like the four mentioned above, there will be no need to worry about lacking the means to handle them; even when words exhibit partialities like those of the four ministers mentioned above, there will be no need to worry about lacking the means to discern them. Your servant's learning is shallow and meager, yet I have been undeservedly graced with the honor of Your Majesty's question. Regarding the four urgent tasks set forth earlier, my exposition of them may not be suited to the times; regarding the partialities of the four ministers discussed later, my rectification of them may not accord with the Way. Yet the sincerity of my single-minded devotion to my Sovereign springs from my innate nature. May Your Majesty pardon my rash folly, deign to show a measure of benevolence, and adopt what I have said; then your foolish servant will be fortunate indeed, and all under Heaven will be fortunate indeed. Having offended against the Imperial Majesty, your servant is overcome with utmost trembling and awe. Your servant respectfully replies.
